title: Playwright Trace Triage
description: 读追踪包对齐快照与网络行找出首个分叉帧
prompt: Triage one visual difference from an offline trace instead of guessing. Import the existing trace v10 archive without contacting a single recorded URL, and keep the archive digest: it identifies members, so two archives with the same file name stay distinct. Page through events by kind, stream, producer ordinal and call id, then read network rows for method, URL, status and timing and console rows for text and location. Headline times are producer monotonic milliseconds per stream, so do not sort trace and network rows onto one axis and do not treat a call id as proof that a before and after pair completed. Align candidate rows to the screencast snapshots by step order, find the first snapshot where the layout diverges from the expected state, then walk back to the request or script that started between the previous snapshot and that one. Name the resource, its origin and its status; if the evidence only narrows the culprit to three candidates, say that and list all three. Keep two limitations in the write-up: a fully read page of facts never proves the recording is complete, and a present-unread member means the archive lists a screenshot or body whose bytes were never validated. Rebuild stack: a short findings note holding the frame index, the responsible URL and the change applied. Acceptance: the diverging frame is named by index with the two screenshots around it, exactly one resource is named or the candidate set is listed with its size, no clock alignment is assumed between streams, completeness stays unknown, and the fix is verified by re-recording the same steps.
notes: Screencast frames are captured on a cadence, not per animation frame, so the diverging snapshot brackets the cause rather than pinpointing it.
A trace viewer is convenient but not evidence; read the archive, and quote member paths so the citation survives.
Unsafe numeric values are not rounded on read, so keep exact literals in sidecars when comparing two traces.

title: Execution Coverage Attribution
description: 用精确覆盖率把可见行为归因到具体函数块
prompt: Attribute a visible effect to code with precise coverage, and bound the claim before making it. Arm coverage through the debugger protocol, then wait for the real armed progress event: performing the interaction before arming yields a table that credits nothing. Perform exactly one interaction, take one resetting sample, then stop coverage and disable the domains you enabled so the next question starts clean. Read the admitted producer function and block ranges with their exclusive end offsets in UTF-16 code units and their execution counts, and keep nested and overlapping counts side by side instead of summing them, because a parent range already contains its children. Record whether the sample carried block granularity: when that flag is false the observation is function-only, branch execution stays unknown, and the write-up has to say so rather than inferring a branch. Accept the distortion openly: arming resets counters and blocks optimised execution, so wall-clock timing from the same window is unusable for performance claims, and a document replacement ends the window and leaves final coverage unavailable. Map counted ranges back to exported source through the script id, then describe the effect as observed in these functions, inferred for the neighbouring code, and unknown elsewhere. Rebuild stack: a coverage table joined to file, line and column, with a claim column. Acceptance: the armed event precedes the action in the log, counts are never summed, function-only samples are labelled, timing taken from the armed window is excluded, and every named function resolves to a source location.
notes: An already loaded script can be absent from a sample and a document replacement can wipe the window entirely; missing coverage is unknown, never zero executions.
Block coverage applies to functions compiled inside the window, so a long-running page may report function-only ranges on the second observation.
Coverage says which code ran, not which code caused the pixel change; pair it with a screenshot pair before writing the conclusion.

title: Event Listener Binding Audit
description: 审计指针与键盘监听的注册来源、阶段与被动标记
prompt: Audit how one control is actually wired before reproducing its feel. Select a single node by CSS selector and list the directly registered listener types with their flags: capture or bubble, passive, once, plus the callback coordinates as a zero-based line with a UTF-16 column in the named resource and the source text digest, so the same handler stays identifiable across reloads. Inspect the node and never dispatch an event, and expect three blind spots: listeners on delegated ancestors, listeners inside closed shadow roots, and framework registries that attach nothing per node. When a click works but the node lists nothing, walk the ancestor chain and record the delegation depth as a number rather than a shrug. Re-inspect after each state change, because hover, focus and open states often add listeners later: capture the binding set cold, after hover, after click and after Escape, then diff the four sets and show which listeners exist only after a state change. Keyboard coverage matters as much as pointer, so check keydown and keyup on the control and on document, and note where a passive flag rules out preventDefault for a custom wheel or touch effect. Report unknown where a call site has no script identity instead of guessing the handler. Rebuild stack: one listener table per control, consumed as the wiring spec. Acceptance: each row has type, phase, passive flag and a source location, delegation is either proven with a depth or marked unknown, the four state snapshots are diffed, the audit dispatches no event itself, and post-interaction bindings are listed apart from startup bindings.
notes: Inspection sees direct registrations only; a delegated ancestor listener is the usual reason a working hover effect appears to have no handler at all.
Never probe bindings by firing synthetic events on a shared browser: a dispatched event can trigger a real write on the reference site.
Capture and passive flags change behaviour far more than the handler body, so record them even when the source is unreadable.

title: Saved-Value Assertion Loop
description: 挑十个可复观测值，让重建结果与原站对齐
prompt: Keep a rebuild honest with a small, re-runnable assertion set. Choose eight to twelve numbers a viewer would notice: a stagger interval, a hero duration, a pin range in pixels, a headline size at two widths, a card radius, a grid gap, a settled opacity and a colour. Capture each from the reference by reading a json_pointer out of a matching 2xx JSON response or a computed style, saving it under a stable name with its unit written beside it; a pointer that names no string or number must fail the step instead of storing a blank. Treat re-observable as a test: the same step replayed on a second reference run and then against the rebuild has to yield the same number, so a value typed in by hand does not qualify. Run the loop with two tolerance classes: exact for counts and enumerations, plus or minus one frame for durations and plus or minus one pixel for sizes, and record which class each row uses. Diff the rebuild against the reference row by row and keep the failures: a duration that misses by 40ms is a finding, not a rounding choice. Report every row the loop cannot observe, such as a value behind a login or set only under one device profile, as unknown with its reason. Rebuild stack: an assertions JSON plus a runner printing pass, fail or unknown per row. Acceptance: every row has a name, unit, value, tolerance class and provenance, the same step produces the row on both sides, no row is hand-entered, failures are reported rather than smoothed, and unobservable rows are marked unknown.
notes: Eight good numbers beat sixty noisy ones; a long assertion file gets muted in the first week and then protects nothing.
Screenshots are withheld whenever a step saves a value marked secret, so plan the assertion loop to use numbers rather than pixels if that path is needed.
Saved values are typed: an id saved as a number is sent back as a number, and a pointer that produces neither a string nor a number fails the step.

title: Screenshot Comparison Memory Budget
description: 按页高切块截图比较，把内存占用压进预算
prompt: Compare long pages without letting the comparison decide your memory ceiling. Measure document height first, then choose a tile height from it instead of taking one full-page shot: a 1440 by 20000 page at four bytes per pixel is about 115 MB per image before two decoded buffers and the RGB to RGBA expansion are counted, while a 1440 by 1600 tile pair stays near 27 MB. Admit each pair against a working-memory budget of 256 MiB and treat a header-valid image that exceeds it as a resource constraint carrying the estimate and the maximum, not as a corrupt file. Tile both captures at identical offsets with a one-pixel overlap guard so a seam is not reported as a difference, hash each tile, compare only tiles whose digests differ, and stream every verdict to disk as it is produced so the run never holds more than one pair in memory. Keep the page at a fixed scroll position while a tile is captured and record the scroll offset beside the tile index, so a re-run cannot compare two different crops. Compare by content digest rather than raw bytes, and count the pixels outside text antialiasing before calling a tile matched: one percent of a tile is an honest threshold, zero is not. Rebuild stack: a tiling script plus a per-tile report file. Acceptance: peak memory stays under the stated budget on a 20000 pixel page, every tile carries index, scroll offset and digest, uncompared or failed tiles are listed instead of silently passing, and the final difference figure is computed from tiles alone.
notes: The budget covers decoder and inflate working memory for one comparison, not process RSS, so the runner still needs headroom for the JSON and base64 strings it holds.
Fixed-position headers repeat in every tile and will be reported as diff noise; mask a stable band or compare only the scrollable region.
Capture and compare at the same device pixel ratio, or every tile differs for a reason that has nothing to do with the rebuild.

title: Storage Fingerprint Diff
description: 指纹化存储键值与写入时机，区分偏好与缓存
prompt: Fingerprint what the site persists, then separate preference writes from cache writes. Snapshot every storage surface after a clean load and again after each of six interactions: local storage, session storage, cookies including HttpOnly names, and the key list of each database. For every key record the surface, the key, the value shape as string length or JSON depth or array length, a SHA-256 over the UTF-8 value, and the step that wrote it. Record fingerprint version 2 beside each digest, because strings with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates hash over a 0xff prefix plus their exact code units, and a digest without that version cannot establish value identity at all. Mark declared secret values as redacted with a null digest and never store their bytes. Diff the two runs key by key: a key that appears only after a click and whose size tracks the interaction is state the rebuild must reproduce, while a key that changes with no interaction and looks like a cache or a nonce is noise to reproduce as structure only, with a generated value. List writes you cannot attribute, such as one set during a redirect or by a worker, as unknown instead of assigning them to the nearest step. Rebuild stack: a fingerprint table plus a small storage module writing only the state that table proves. Acceptance: every key has surface, shape, digest and writing step, version 2 appears on each digest, preferences and cache are separated by a stated rule, unattributed writes stay unknown, and no secret value is retained.
notes: Legacy captures without the version marker have to be compared as unknown, including old against old, so recapture both sides before drawing a conclusion.
Empty or fully redacted storage has its own comparison semantics; treating it as an unchanged surface hides a real difference.
Storage order is not stable across runs, so diff a sorted key list rather than raw dumps.

title: Third-Party Script Attribution
description: 按外部域名拆解脚本体积、阻塞与动效归属
prompt: Split first-party from third-party cost before copying a single line of motion code. List every external origin in the capture with its transfer bytes, decoded bytes, request count and cache status, then classify each as render-blocking in the head, deferred, or lazy after interaction, using observed timings rather than assumptions about where the tag sits. Identify which origin actually drives the effect you want: a 40 KB animation library on the primary origin and a 400 KB analytics bundle that never touches the canvas belong in different columns. State the authority behind each number, because a passive devtools attachment that observes without driving, and a driven scenario that clicks and captures step snapshots, record different facts and carry different scopes. Keep the rebuild free of code you cannot licence: for every library record name, version, licence and file size, and prefer MIT or Apache-2.0 equivalents you can vendor and pin. Where a third-party script is entangled with the visual result, say so and describe the minimum behaviour to reimplement rather than shipping the vendor bundle. Record what you could not see, such as an origin blocked before it responded or a fetch that never produced a body, as unknown. Rebuild stack: a per-origin table plus a vendored dependency list with licences. Acceptance: every external origin has bytes, blocking class and purpose, exactly one origin is named as the motion driver, no unlicensed script is copied into the rebuild, and blocked or unattributed origins are marked unknown.
notes: An analytics or tag-manager bundle can inject the animation script later, so the origin that loads a file is often not the origin that authored it.
Bytes from a warm cache flatter every third party; measure with a disabled cache and note the device pixel ratio alongside it.
Attribution is a sharing rule, not a legal opinion: if the licence is unclear, replace the library rather than argue about it.

title: Font Load Attestation
description: 枚举实际渲染的字面，量出字体回退造成的位移
prompt: Goal: prove which faces actually painted instead of assuming a webfont arrived. Open the reference at 1440x900 in a disposable profile and throttle to 1.6 Mbps so the swap window stays visible, then read document.fonts as a FontFaceSet: log every FontFace's family, style, weight, unicodeRange, display, status and loaded count, plus document.fonts.check() for the split headline, body and caption runs. Record the timeline: navigation start, the first frame with no text, the first frame with fallback glyphs, the first frame with the intended face, and document.fonts.ready. Compare screenshots taken 0 and 1500 ms after DOMContentLoaded: identical boxes with different glyph shapes is a FOUT signature, an empty box that fills is FOIT. For each family capture the @font-face src list, the preload or preconnect that fetched it, transfer bytes, and whether a size-adjust or metric-override declaration sits on the fallback. Derive the layout delta by measuring a 60-character line in both states to the pixel, plus the line-height difference; that number is the reservation the rebuild needs. Never substitute a licensed face you did not clear; record provenance per file. Rebuild stack: local woff2 with font-display: swap, one size-adjust value solved from the measured delta, and a preload for the single face used above the fold. Acceptance: every painted face has an observed status line, the FOUT or FOIT verdict names the two screenshots it rests on, the fallback delta is within 2 px after size-adjust, and each face without a licence is marked unknown rather than shipped.
notes: A face in status loaded only means the bytes decoded; whether it painted is a separate question answered by the screenshot pair.
Reading document.fonts.check() before the set is ready returns a misleading answer, so gate every probe on the ready promise.
Subsetting and variable axes change transfer size far more than the display policy does; measure both before choosing a fallback strategy.

title: Media Layer Recovery
description: 还原首屏媒体层的构建方式，给出同观感的最省重建
prompt: Recover what a hero media layer actually is before rebuilding one frame of it. Attach to the page over a loopback CDP endpoint and run a single declarative scenario: goto, wait for a page-specific ready marker, screenshot, wait 1200 ms, screenshot, then a third shot after the expected loop point, with network events captured across the whole window. Classify the layer from that evidence alone: an autoplay muted inline video (record currentTime drift between the last two shots and whether the loop restarts it), a scroll-scrubbed video (currentTime bound to scroll offset, sampled at four positions), a numbered image sequence (count sequential frame files and their encode), a sprite sheet (background-position steps against frame count), a CSS gradient mesh, or a WebGL texture. For each candidate record source resolution, poster URL and poster frame, preload value, codec container, transfer and decoded bytes, the container's CSS size, and any mobile crop requested by a 390-wide device profile. Tag every fact observed, inferred or unknown; the decode path is unknown unless the events prove it. Rebuild stack: a re-encoded AVIF or WebP frame sequence preloaded 30 percent ahead of first scroll, preload=metadata with playsinline muted loop for video, an LQIP poster, and a still image fallback for reduced motion. Capture only what an ordinary page load serves; a gated asset is recorded as unavailable and left alone. Acceptance: two runs of the same scenario classify the layer identically, the poster is visible in the first screenshot, largest contentful paint stays under 1.5 s, and every asset carries a provenance line.
notes: A network log shows what loaded, not what the section needs; scrub and hover before trusting a single-shot inventory.
Scroll-scrubbed video stalls on iOS Safari, so budget a frame sequence or poster path even when the reference gets away without one.
Reusing reference footage is a licensing question, not a technical one; record provenance per file and substitute where rights are unclear.

title: Consent and Overlay State Capture
description: 抓取首访才出现的浮层，记录层叠、焦点与关闭路径
prompt: Capture the overlays a clean first visit shows, and the ones it hides behind interaction. Start from empty storage in a provider-owned browser so no consent choice is remembered, load the page at 1440x900, and screenshot at 0, 400 and 1200 ms before any click. Then run a declared step sequence: dismiss the consent banner, open the newsletter modal from the footer, close it with its own close control, and reopen it with Escape as the exit. Capture DOM, accessibility tree, screenshot and the active element after every step. For each overlay record role (dialog, complementary, region), aria-modal, labelledby targets, z-index with its stacking-context parent, bounding box, whether focus is trapped, which element takes focus on open, which dismissal targets actually work, and what each panel does to what sits below it: compare the hero's top offset and the scrollbar gutter before and after. A panel that appeared and closed before the observation window armed is unknown, not absent, so every row carries an observed, inferred or unknown tag. Rebuild stack: a native dialog element driven by a small state machine, a focus trap only while modal, a scroll lock that reserves the gutter width, and a consent banner that does not push the header. Acceptance: the inventory names every panel with its stacking number, focus return is asserted after each close, layout below moves less than 1 px across an open-close cycle, and every panel the capture never showed is listed as unknown.
notes: Consent tooling often injects its own shadow root and iframe, so an empty page DOM is a boundary observation, not proof that nothing rendered.
Focus that returns to the body instead of the trigger is the most common overlay defect; assert the target, not just that focus exists.
Two overlays can both claim a trap; check the stacking context parent before believing the larger z-index.

title: Layout Shift Budget Capture
description: 按元素记录布局位移，算出重建需要预留的空间
prompt: Attribute layout shift to nodes rather than to a page average. Load the reference in a disposable profile at 1440x900 with a 4x CPU throttle and a 1.6 Mbps link, install a PerformanceObserver for layout-shift through an init script so it is armed before the first paint, and read buffered entries to catch what fired earlier. For each entry record value, startTime, hadRecentInput, and for each shifted source node its selector path, previousRect, currentRect, the pixel delta, and the suspected cause class: media without intrinsic size, a late webfont, an injected banner, a placeholder replaced by real content, or an animation on a layout property. Sum contributions per node and rank them; anything above 0.05 of the total earns its own budget line. Match each shift to the request that landed just before it in the network events, then state the reservation the rebuild needs: explicit width and height or aspect-ratio for media, a min-height for banners, size-adjust plus metric overrides for fonts, and transform or opacity instead of top and height. Re-measure the score after the fix under the identical throttle and report both numbers side by side, each tagged observed, inferred or unknown. Acceptance: the clone's per-node shift total is at most 0.02 at 1440x900, no single node exceeds 0.01, no shift is attributed to user input, and every original shift has either a reservation or an explicit unknown reason.
notes: Buffered observer entries report what already happened; without buffered: true the first and largest shift is simply missed.
A shift caused by a font swap can be fixed only by metric overrides, and a shift caused by a banner needs a reserved slot, not a smaller banner.
Throttle consistently or the numbers are not comparable between reference and clone.

title: Same-Document Navigation Capture
description: 记录同文档导航的替换、滚动与播报，并验证深链直开
prompt: Capture client-side navigation instead of assuming pages. With the scenario provider attached, arm an observation window of 10 seconds, click the primary nav link, and record the ordered page and history events; do not infer a push from a URL change alone. For each same-document step capture the URL before and after, whether the entry was pushed or replaced, scrollY at both points, which subtrees were removed and inserted by normalized structure rather than text, which nodes kept identity, the focus target, the document title, any live-region announcement, and the covering transition with its duration in milliseconds. Then fetch two deep routes directly with JavaScript disabled: a full render means the routing is server-compatible, a shell means the rebuild needs prerendering or a static document per route. Compare two captures by exact step id to see whether back and forward replay identical state; a step with no counterpart or a changed action kind is an alignment failure, never a match. Treat every route absent from the walk as unknown, and tag each captured fact observed or inferred so no row stays untagged. Rebuild stack: History API plus an explicit route table, one container transition of 180 to 320 ms, focus moved to the new h1, a live region asserted once per swap, and a prerendered document for each deep route. Acceptance: direct load of two deep routes renders the same first screen as the in-app click, back and forward restore scroll within 4 px, the swap is announced exactly once, and the coverage table lists which routes were never visited.
notes: A URL that changes without a history entry is the norm in replace-style routers and breaks back on the first click.
Scroll restoration is usually app code, not the browser; capture it explicitly or the clone will jump to the top.
The observation window matters: navigation finished after it closes leaves the end state unknown.

title: Shadow DOM Inspection Bounds
description: 界定封闭影子根的取证边界，只描述能证明的部分
prompt: Establish how far inspection reaches before describing any widget's internals. Pick the custom elements on the page, such as a search field, a carousel and a player wrapper, and for each check whether shadowRoot is non-null in the page context. For open roots, walk them once and record the host tag, mode, nested root count, adopted stylesheets and the accessible name the host exposes outward. For closed roots, record the same host-level facts and stop there: no guessed class names, no invented markup, no injected script to force a root open. Use the accessibility tree as the honest external view, because it reports the roles, names and states the host publishes regardless of shadow mode. Then check delegation: whether listeners sit on ancestors rather than the inner control, and whether the events that cross the boundary are composed, read from a passive listener log rather than from source guesses. Write the result as a coverage table with one row per widget and a verdict of observed, partially observed or unknown. Rebuild stack: a custom element with an open root, ::part and custom properties as the styling contract, and slots so downstream code never needs shadow internals. Acceptance: every widget has one row, closed roots are marked unknown with host facts retained, no claim cites markup the capture did not return, and the rebuild exposes the same accessible names at 1440 and 390.
notes: Declarative shadow DOM arrives in the parsed HTML, so a root can exist before any script runs; check the document, not only the element upgrade path.
Attach-mode inspection does not widen into closed roots, and an unobserved interior stays unknown no matter how familiar the component looks.
Delegated listeners on the host are the usual reason a click test passes while the inner control appears dead.

source.ref: morluto/rea — docs/guides/web/web-runtime.md (bounds and verification, delegated listeners)

title: Canvas Draw-Call Budget
description: 量出画布每帧的绘制调用与上传量，折算成重建预算
prompt: Measure what a canvas hero costs per frame before deciding how to rebuild it. Attach passively, hook the WebGL and WebGL2 draw functions through an init script so the counters exist before the scene compiles, and sample for a fixed 3 second window with the pointer resting still. Record per frame: drawArrays, drawElements and instanced call counts, texture and buffer upload bytes, program switches, the renderer string from the debug renderer info extension, canvas width and height in device pixels against CSS size, devicePixelRatio, the requestAnimationFrame interval, and the longest frame in the window. Turn that into a budget: a 16.7 ms frame at 60 Hz leaves roughly 8 ms for the scene after style, layout and composite, so state the target as calls per frame, uploads per second and megapixels per frame. Note whether the page clamps devicePixelRatio at 2, renders at half resolution and upscales, and pauses the loop on visibility or intersection changes. Where a counter cannot be observed, say so instead of estimating silently. Rebuild stack: instanced geometry, one atlas texture, a clamped pixel ratio, and a loop that stops when the canvas leaves the viewport. Acceptance: the counter table covers at least 180 frames, the budget states calls, uploads and megapixels, the clone holds under 8 ms of frame time at 1440x900, and every unobserved metric is listed as unknown.
notes: Hooking after the scene compiles misses program creation and the first texture uploads, which are often the most expensive frame.
Draw-call counts mean little without the pixel area they cover; report megapixels with the calls or the budget is not comparable.
The other two vendors are MIT or Apache licensed, but a debug renderer string is a hint, not a capability report.

title: Preload and Priority Hint Audit
description: 梳理预加载与优先级提示，按原顺序复现关键四资源
prompt: Rebuild a hint graph deliberately instead of hoping the browser guesses well. Load the reference at 1440x900 with cache disabled and a fresh profile, and record every request with its initiator, priority and start time. From the document head extract preload, preconnect, dns-prefetch, modulepreload and prefetch links with their as, type, crossorigin and media values, plus any fetchpriority attribute on images, scripts and frames. Identify, from the observed start times, the four assets that begin first and what pulled each one: a preload link, an early script, the parser, or a stylesheet's font rule. Price each hint: a preconnect to an origin the page never touches, a crossorigin mismatch that forces a second fetch, a preload with the wrong as that downloads twice, a preload competing with the largest paint. Then write the head for the clone so the same first four starts recur, keeping the hint count at or below six inside the first 20 KB of markup, and verify by re-running the capture with identical settings. Only requests the public page makes belong in the graph; anything behind a session stays unknown instead of being inferred from a hint. Rebuild stack: one preload for the hero image with imagesrcset and high fetchpriority, one modulepreload for the entry chunk, a single preconnect to the font or media origin actually used, and prefetch deferred to idle. Acceptance: the clone's first four asset starts match the reference order, no asset downloads twice, no hint targets an origin that is never requested, and the hint list ships beside the capture.
notes: Hints are advisory: the browser may reorder them, so verify the resulting start order rather than the declared one.
A duplicate download is the classic signature of a preload whose as or crossorigin does not match the real request.
Priority collapses on a slow connection; judge the graph on a throttled profile, not on a fast local one.

title: Console and Network Noise Floor
description: 记录参考站自带的报错，作为重建的噪声基线
prompt: Record the errors a reference already produces so a rebuild is judged against the same floor. Load the page at 1440x900 with a disposable profile, empty storage and no extensions, then observe for a 10 second window while performing one standard tour: initial load, one scroll to the footer, one click on the primary call to action, one resize to 390 wide. Collect every console entry with level, source URL and line, every page error with its stack, every failed request with status and reason, and every policy violation report. Classify each into expected noise, tolerated noise and real failure: an analytics or consent script throwing on a blocked third party is expected, a broken module import or a 404 on a render-critical asset is a real failure. Keep the classified list with the capture and with the browser build string, because a different build can change the list without the site changing. Then decide what the clone should do with each line: reproduce, silence, or unknown with a reason, and tag every decision observed or inferred. Rebuild stack: a small assertion script that loads the clone, applies the same tour, and fails the build when a new unclassified console error or a render-critical failure appears, while the allowed list is committed next to it. Acceptance: the inventory covers console, page error, failed request and violation families, every entry carries a class and a decision, the clone produces no real failures, and each reproduced entry names the capture it came from.
notes: Chasing zero errors on a site whose consent stack always throws wastes days; the floor is the honest target.
Third-party failures change with blocked domains and geography, so record the environment with the list.
An unclassified new error is the useful signal; a growing allowlist with no reasons defeats the point.

title: Reconstruction Obligation Ledger
description: 逐条登记重建依赖的断言，标注已观察、推断与未知
prompt: Keep every assumption a rebuild rests on in one auditable table. Create a ledger with columns: claim id, claim text, category (structure, token, motion, media, network, behaviour), status of observed, inferred or unknown, evidence pointer (capture id, step id, selector, byte range), a confidence note, and the single capture that would upgrade an unknown to observed. Fill it from existing evidence before writing code: a computed style read on the live page is observed, a duration guessed from a minified variable name is inferred, an interaction nobody triggered is unknown. For each unknown state the cheapest settling probe, such as one more scenario step, a longer observation window, a second viewport, or a request body. Let no claim in status unknown be consumed by the build without a visible fallback, and record the number you chose when you hardcode one. Re-run the capture after each probe so rows change state through a diff rather than from memory. Do not close a gap by asserting access you do not have: a login wall, a paywall or a protected stream stays unknown and its row says why. Rebuild stack: one JSON ledger committed beside the code, a rule that every token and timeline value cites a claim id, and a build check that fails when an unknown claim is used without a fallback. Acceptance: every style token and timeline number maps to a claim id, no unknown appears as fact, observed, inferred and unknown counts print on every build, and each unknown names one concrete capture to upgrade it.
notes: The ledger decays the moment it lives in someone's notes; commit it and let the build read it.
Inferred claims are where silent drift starts, because they look as solid as observed ones in a code review.
Counts printed per build make an unexamined gap visible without anyone reading the whole table.

source.ref: morluto/rea — docs/reference/reconstruction-obligation-ledgers.md; docs/reference/limits-and-recovery.md (claim states and recovery limits)

title: WebGL Context Loss Capture
description: 抓取上下文丢失与恢复路径，含无 WebGL 时的兜底
prompt: Capture the recovery path a WebGL hero uses, not only its first frame. Attach to the page, arm on the canvas, then force the two events the rebuild must survive: call loseContext() through the lose-context extension from the page console, screenshot at 0 and 800 ms, then restoreContext() and screenshot again at 200, 800 and 2000 ms. Record which listeners sit on the canvas for the lost and restored events, whether the lost event is cancelled, which resources are rebuilt (textures, buffers, programs, render targets), and what the canvas shows in between: a frozen last frame, a flat colour, a poster or a spinner. Then load the same URL with WebGL disabled and capture what replaces the canvas: a static image, a CSS composition, an empty box. Note whether the scene pauses when the document is hidden, and whether the restored frame needs a user gesture before it draws. Tag each step observed, and leave any path you could not trigger as unknown together with the command you tried. Rebuild stack: a renderer with explicit lost and restored handlers that stop the loop, mark GPU resources dirty and re-upload on restore, plus a fallback image chosen by feature detection before the module loads. Acceptance: both forced events appear in the evidence with timestamps, the clone restores within 2 s with no blank frame after the first restored paint, the fallback renders without WebGL, and no entry claims a state the observation never reached.
notes: Losing the context by hand is the only reliable test; waiting for a driver reset means shipping untested recovery.
Restoring without re-uploading resources yields a black canvas that still reports a healthy renderer, the most common version of this bug.
The renderer library is MIT, but the extension that simulates loss is vendor behaviour and may differ across browsers.

source.ref: morluto/rea — docs/guides/web/browser-observation.md (non-goals and threat model); docs/guides/web/web-runtime.md

title: Service Worker Cache Layer
description: 判定服务工作线程的缓存层，识别陈旧资源签名
prompt: Find out whether a worker sits between the page and the network before trusting any capture. Record the service worker policy the scenario environment reported, then on an attached browser check the registrations list and the controller, and read the worker script URL with its scope. Enumerate what it stores by walking Cache Storage: cache names, entry counts and total bytes per cache, without reading bodies that belong to another origin. Characterise the strategy with two loads, the first with the worker active and storage cleared, the second with the same worker and warm caches, comparing which requests reached the network, which were answered from cache, the response time for both, and whether an older build was served. Look for the stale signature: a hashed asset in the document that disagrees with the current reference list, a navigation answered offline from an old shell, a versioned cache that was never deleted. Reproduce first-load behaviour with registration blocked and storage cleared so the rebuild is measured against the origin rather than somebody's cache. Capture only public responses and label any storage you could not read as unknown, tagging each entry observed or inferred. Rebuild stack: a versioned precache keyed by build id, network-first for documents, stale-while-revalidate only for images, and an activate step that deletes superseded caches. Acceptance: the inventory names script, scope and every cache with entry count, the two loads are compared, the stale signature is found or explicitly absent, and an offline reload serves the current build id.
notes: A worker can answer a request with a year-old body while the network panel shows a 200, so request-based captures need the worker state recorded.
Clients claim control only after activate and a reload; measuring on the first navigation often reports no controller.
Blocking registration is what makes a rebuild comparable, because a warm cache hides real network cost.

title: Reference Drift Scan
description: 按周期重跑取证并分类内容、布局与动效漂移
prompt: Re-run the reference capture on a schedule and treat each difference as a finding. Freeze a baseline from one scenario file with stable step ids, two viewports at 1440x900 and 390x844, one device scale factor and one recorded browser build; store screenshots, normalized DOM, computed values and the request list in a dated folder. Re-run the identical scenario after 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, comparing step by step: a step whose id is missing, duplicated, or whose action kind changed is an alignment failure and proves neither sameness nor change. Classify every difference as content (copy, price, a swapped image), layout (a moved section, changed spacing, a shifted breakpoint) or motion (a duration, easing or scroll threshold), and attach a magnitude in pixels or milliseconds. Record what stayed identical as well, because a completely empty diff on a live site usually means the capture broke, not that the site froze, and tag every row observed, inferred or unknown so a change of class is never confused with a change of confidence. Keep the baseline immutable: write a new dated snapshot every run and diff against the previous one instead of overwriting in place. Rebuild stack: a scheduled job that captures and diffs, a tolerance of 1 percent of pixels for anti-aliasing noise, a report listing class, magnitude and step id, and a hard warning when a run writes fewer artifacts than the baseline. Acceptance: every drift row names a step id and a class, alignment failures are reported apart from differences, the first baseline is never mutated, and a run with missing artifacts fails loudly rather than reporting a clean diff.
notes: Comparing against a rolling latest capture hides slow drift; always diff against the frozen original as well as the previous run.
Text antialiasing and image decoding differences produce noise that a pixel tolerance handles and a structural diff does not.
A reference site that serves experiments will drift by design; record the variant so a redesign does not look like a regression.

title: Screenshot to UI Blueprint Decompose
description: 先拆区块、控件状态与数值清单，再写代码
prompt: Replicate this interface from evidence, not memory. You have screenshots of the target at 1440, 1024 and 390 px wide. Step 1, blueprint: write ui/blueprint.md before touching code. List the page as ordered blocks (header, hero, feature grid, footer) and give each one its content, measured box (content column width, padding, gaps, items per row) and the elements inside it. Name every interactive control with a kind (link, menu, tab, toggle, field, carousel), and for each list states (rest, hover, focus-visible, pressed, open, loading, error, empty, disabled) with what it looks like in each. Step 2, mechanics sheet: write ui/mechanics.json as version 1 with a values array, each entry a name, group, value, unit and either a source or estimated true. Put in every number and rule that shapes behaviour: durations, delays, easings, scroll thresholds, breakpoints, content widths, radii, tap target sizes. Cite each to a screenshot file plus crop region, or mark it estimated. Step 3, unknowns: list what the evidence cannot settle (off-screen states, hover on touch, real data volume) and what would settle it. Step 4, craft: plain HTML, CSS custom properties and vanilla JS, one block per section, tokens only, no inline sizes. Acceptance self-tests: every control in the blueprint exists in the build with all its listed states; every number in mechanics.json appears as a token, not a literal; a second agent could rebuild the page from blueprint.md alone; no unknown is stated as fact.
notes: One width is not evidence: the same section can be a 3-column grid at 1440 and a stack at 390, and differences at the middle width reveal the breakpoint.
Mark estimated values explicitly; a plausible-looking invented spacing value is the most common silent clone failure.
The blueprint is a deliverable, not scratch work: reviewers and later agents rebuild from it, so keep it in the repo.

title: Design Token Extraction From Screenshots
description: 从截图量出配色、字号、间距、圆角与阴影令牌
prompt: Turn a screenshot set into the design tokens the target uses, before styling a single component. Work in this order. Evidence: for each of the three widths, crop the page into regions (header, hero, cards, footer) and sample the dominant fill, text colour and border colour per region; record hex values, never names. Type: measure pixel height of the top heading, subheads, body and caption, plus line-height from baseline to baseline, weight and letter-spacing; note the font family and its fallback stack. Space: measure gaps between blocks, card padding, grid gutters and the content column max-width; snap to the nearest 4 px step while keeping the measured value in a comment. Shape: radii for cards, buttons, inputs and pills; border widths; shadow offset, blur, spread and alpha. Emit tokens.css with custom properties for colour, type scale, space, radius, shadow and container width, plus tokens.json holding value, role and the crop each came from. Compute contrast for every text-on-surface pair and fail anything below 4.5 to 1 for body text and 3 to 1 for large text or controls; where the original itself fails, keep the measured token but add a compliant alternative. Acceptance self-tests: grepping the build for hex colours or raw px outside tokens.css returns nothing; every token in tokens.json is used at least once; rendered heading sizes and section padding match the measurements within 2 px at each width.
notes: Snapshot colours from a PNG, not from a designer's memory: JPEG screenshots shift hue, so capture lossless or average a flat region.
Snap to a grid but keep the raw measurement visible; an unsnapped 22 px gap usually means the real token is 20 px plus a border.
Contrast failures in the original are common in dark themes; ship the faithful token and a compliant sibling rather than silently changing the look.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md; crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (capture.json design tokens and per-width layouts)

title: Interaction State Machine Map
description: 把每个控件写成状态、事件、守卫与转场表
prompt: Map every interactive control as an explicit state machine before implementing it. For the dropdown, modal, tabs, accordion, toggle and carousel visible in the target, write a table with columns: state, trigger event, guard, next state, side effect, and visible difference with a screenshot crop. Cover at least rest, hover, focus-visible, pressed, open, opening, closing, loading, success, error, empty and disabled. Name timing explicitly, for example closed to open on click or Enter, 180 ms fade plus 8 px rise, focus moves to the first item; Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger, and the exit animation finishes before the node unmounts. Implement each component as a small finite-state machine: one state enum, one transition function, and CSS driven by a data-state attribute so styling cannot drift from logic. Inputs are pointer, keyboard, focus and media query; guards ignore a second click during closing. Acceptance self-tests: scripted runs fire each transition and assert the state attribute, ARIA expanded, selected and disabled, and focus position; every state in the table is reachable in the build; no input path leaves a stale open state; a transition trace log shows no double fire; a keyboard-only run completes the same flows as the pointer run.
notes: Most clone bugs are stale state, not styling: a menu that stays open after route change or a modal that traps focus after closing.
Exit animations must not be skipped; unmounting immediately is the single most noticeable difference from a premium original.
Testing only click paths hides keyboard gaps; drive the same machine with Enter, Space, Escape and Tab.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (opened states, paired state checks); docs/pitfalls.md

title: Motion Timing Token System
description: 按帧量出时长、缓动与错峰，生成动效令牌
prompt: Derive a motion system from evidence instead of guessing durations. Screen-record the target, step frames, and measure the enter duration, exit duration, delay between siblings, distance travelled, and whether opacity, transform or layout animates. Sort the measurements into token tiers: instant 80 to 120 ms for press feedback, control 150 to 200 ms for hover and focus, enter 240 to 320 ms for panels and modals, exit about 65 percent of enter, and ambient loops 6 to 12 s. Define easing tokens: standard for in-place change, decelerate for entrances, accelerate for exits, and a spring for draggable elements with explicit stiffness and damping. Express stagger as a per-item delay with a total cap. Implement with CSS transitions and keyframes, animating transform, opacity and colour only, and add a reduced-motion branch that keeps state changes while removing travel and loops. Acceptance self-tests: every token is exercised by a named element in a motion manifest; a timeline dump of the rebuilt interaction matches the measured durations within 20 percent; nothing animates width, height, top or left; there is no layout shift after load; with prefers-reduced-motion enabled all content stays reachable and no loop runs; a frame check shows no long task during the heaviest entrance.
notes: Frame-step a recording rather than eyeballing it; 150 ms and 220 ms feel different and the difference is invisible without frames.
Exit being faster than enter is what makes an interface feel responsive; symmetric durations read as sluggish.
Animating transform and opacity keeps work on the compositor; animating layout properties causes jank on mid-range phones.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (hover ease, popup fade, wheel step); crates/ai/src/rebuild/brief.rs (noise regions that animate)

title: Color and Material Surface System
description: 重建表面层级、玻璃与光影材质，逐通道比对
prompt: Rebuild the surface and material language, not just the colours. From the crops, build a five-step surface ladder from page background to the highest floating card, recording the measured hex and alpha for each. Identify the materials actually in use: flat fill, translucent glass with a background blur, gradient mesh, grain or noise overlay, hairline inner highlight, outer glow, and image scrim. For each material write a recipe with exact values (blur radius, saturation, noise opacity, gradient stops, highlight width, shadow stack) and the layer order that produces it. Implement with CSS custom properties and layered backgrounds or box-shadows, one utility class per material, and a single light model so shadows fall in one direction. Never fake elevation with a border alone. Acceptance self-tests: sample the rebuilt screenshot at the same crop coordinates and require each surface within 3 per channel of the original; the surface ladder must be strictly ordered in luminance in both light and dark modes; text contrast stays at or above 4.5 to 1 on every surface, including glass over media; a 4x zoom crop shows no banding and no blurry text; material classes are reused with zero material values inlined in markup.
notes: Glass without a fallback becomes unreadable over bright images; add a solid or heavy-blur fallback layer.
Grain overlays must be tiled and tiny or they destroy text sharpness at 1x.
If the original uses licensed imagery as the material itself, rebuild the gradient and noise, not the asset.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (backgrounds, text colours, per-channel colour tolerance); docs/design-system.md (surfaces, edges, focus ring)

title: Hero Section Faithful Rebuild
description: 按三档宽度重建首屏：网格、字体断行与主按钮状态
prompt: Rebuild this hero section faithfully at 1440, 1024 and 390 px. Blueprint first: the hero as a grid with named areas (eyebrow, headline, subhead, primary and secondary action, social proof, media or background layer), the content column max-width, the vertical padding, and the gap scale between elements. Record exact type: heading size, line-height, weight, tracking and the number of lines at each width, plus where the headline breaks; the same for subhead and labels. Capture states: primary action rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible, loading; secondary action the same; any media hover or autoplay loop. Build with semantic HTML, tokens from the extracted sheet, and one element per grid area so blocks can be reordered without breaking. Timing: hero entrance stagger of 60 to 80 ms per line, total under 600 ms, transform and opacity only. Acceptance self-tests: the hero occupies the same first-fold height within 24 px at 1440x900; the headline breaks on the same words; both actions are reachable by Tab with a visible focus ring; the largest image is lazy unless it is the LCP, in which case it is preloaded with correct dimensions; no layout shift from font or media load; screenshot diff at each width with self-changing regions masked.
notes: Headline line breaks are a design decision; letting text reflow freely is the fastest way to look like a different site.
Set explicit image width and height or the LCP element shifts and the hero jumps on load.
Rebuild the copy rather than copying the original's marketing text and logos unless you own it.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/brief.rs (match capture tokens exactly); crates/ai/src/rebuild/study.rs (multi-width capture and opened states)

title: Scroll Storytelling Build
description: 按进度百分比建滚动时间线，逐段对齐参考帧
prompt: Build the scroll story from a measured timeline, not from feel. Blueprint: list each scroll block with its height in viewports, whether it is pinned, and what changes between progress 0 and 1 (transform, opacity, clip, text swap, camera). For every block write a mapping table: progress 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 against the expected visual state, each row cited to a frame captured from the target. Implement with a sticky container plus one requestAnimationFrame loop that reads scroll position once per frame, lerps toward the target progress with a damping factor, and writes transforms and CSS custom properties. Avoid a scroll listener per element, and never animate layout properties. Snap progress into discrete keyframes where the original steps rather than glides. Acceptance self-tests: capture the rebuilt page at the five progress points per block and compare with the reference frames, with section order and pin durations matching; scrolling backwards is symmetric; the page throws no console errors and no content is lost without JavaScript; reduced motion collapses the story to static sections with all copy present; no horizontal scrollbar appears at any width; a performance pass shows no layout thrash and no long task above 50 ms while scrolling.
notes: Lerp one shared progress value instead of animating each element independently, or the sections drift apart on fast wheels.
Pin durations are usually set in viewport heights; hardcoding pixels breaks on short laptop screens.
Always keep a no-JS or reduced-motion reading path; scroll effects that hide content are an accessibility failure.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (per-width layout and block measurements); crates/setup/src/skill.md (predict, then verify)

title: Gesture and Input Mechanics
description: 定义拖拽阈值、速度、惯性、取消与键盘等价操作
prompt: Recreate the input mechanics of the target precisely: pointer, touch, wheel and keyboard. For each interactive surface write an input spec with recognised gestures, activation threshold in pixels or milliseconds, direction constraints, velocity units in px per ms, inertia decay, rubber-band resistance, snap points, cancel conditions (pointercancel, pointerup outside, Escape), and the keyboard equivalent of every pointer action. Separate what moves what: a cursor-follow highlight uses a fixed transform with a lerp, drag uses pointer capture and translate3d, wheel uses a normalized delta with a small dead zone, and touch must never trap page scroll unless the element is a deliberate horizontal track with a clear affordance. Implement with Pointer Events only, one shared drag controller, and requestAnimationFrame for smoothing. Acceptance self-tests: synthetic pointer sequences confirm the dead zone, snapping and inertia settling within 400 ms; Escape and pointercancel always release state; touch targets are at least 44 px; the same result is reachable by keyboard with visible focus; the element does not hijack vertical scroll; a swipe on a 390 px viewport never triggers an accidental drag; a state dump after each gesture shows the controller returned to idle.
notes: Pointer events cover mouse, pen and touch in one path; separate touch handlers are where double-fire bugs live.
Never set touch-action none on a large scrollable region; scope it to the draggable track only.
Inertia with no decay cap overshoots the last slide; clamp velocity and snap on release.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/pitfalls.md (input and state edge cases); crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (states opened by real interaction)

title: 3D and WebGL Scene Craft
description: 先写场景蓝图再建 WebGL：相机、材质、状态与降级
prompt: Recreate the 3D or WebGL moment with a scene blueprint before writing any shader. Record from the target: camera field of view, approximate distance, orbit or fixed rig, the geometry inventory and proportions, materials (metalness, roughness, transmission, emissive), light count and direction, environment or lighting probe, any post effect (bloom, grain, vignette, chromatic aberration), and the still frame it holds at idle. Then define states as a small machine: idle loop, pointer parallax, hover accent, scroll progress, loading, error, reduced-motion still. Implement with three.js: one renderer capped at devicePixelRatio 2, a single animation loop, instancing for repeats, compressed textures, and a pause when the canvas leaves the viewport or the tab is hidden. Acceptance self-tests: a still frame captured at the same camera matches the reference crop in composition and colour; frame time stays under 16.7 ms on integrated graphics; no console warnings; the canvas is keyboard-focusable and labelled, with every critical word outside it in real text; when WebGL is unavailable or reduced motion is set, a static poster with identical layout replaces the scene; no layout shift on first paint; no model, HDRI or texture with unclear licensing is used.
notes: Cap pixel ratio at 2; uncapped DPR on phones is the most common cause of a failed 3D hero.
A poster fallback is not optional: some corporate browsers and accessibility settings have no WebGL.
Never ship a downloaded environment map or model without a recorded licence; generate or commission instead.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/brief.rs (poster and picture fallbacks, no unlicensed assets); docs/pitfalls.md (runtime and performance traps)

title: Micro-interaction Polish Pass
description: 逐个打磨按钮、提示与加载反馈的微动效数值
prompt: Polish the micro-interactions that make an interface feel crafted, each one specified with numbers. Inventory from the target every small feedback: button press, hover lift, icon or label swap, toggle knob, checkbox tick, field focus, inline validation shake, tooltip delay, toast enter and exit, skeleton to content crossfade, row hover reveal, copy confirmation. For each write trigger, property animated, from and to values, duration, easing, delay, and what it must never do (block input, shift layout, fire twice). Implement with CSS transitions on transform, opacity and colour, using a small JavaScript helper only for timing sequences such as label swap or toast queues. Keep one shared set of easing and duration tokens so nothing drifts. Acceptance self-tests: a staged capture at 0, 60, 140 and 300 ms after activation matches the reference crops; rapid double activation leaves no stuck state; every animated control still reports its state to assistive technology; pointer and keyboard activation produce identical feedback; reduced motion swaps travel for a short opacity change; removing all animation leaves the UI fully usable, proving animation decorates rather than gates.
notes: Polish is budgeted by attention: the primary action and destructive action deserve the detail, every hover row does not.
Toasts must queue and self-dismiss except errors, which should stay until dismissed.
Skeletons must match the final content shape or the crossfade reads as a jump.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (hover ease, toast rules, spinner guidance); crates/ai/src/rebuild/brief.rs (fix the biggest visible difference first)

title: Responsive and Accessibility Parity
description: 按真实断点做响应式，并用可测断言校验无障碍
prompt: Make the replica responsive and accessible to the same standard as the original, measured rather than asserted. First extract breakpoints from evidence: capture at 390, 768, 1024 and 1440 px, and note exactly where sections stack, the grid drops a column, and the navigation becomes a menu button. Record per width: page width versus viewport, heading and body sizes, section padding, items per row and content column. Build mobile-first with a small set of breakpoint tokens so each layout switch is one rule rather than a scatter of overrides. Then parity: one header, navigation, main and footer landmark; heading order with no skipped level; alt text or an explicit decorative role for media; every control named; form fields with real labels; page language set; focus order following visual order; a skip link; focus ring at 3 to 1 against every surface; text at 4.5 to 1; touch targets at least 44 px; usable at 200 percent zoom. Acceptance self-tests: assert page width never exceeds viewport at any tested width where the original does not scroll; landmark counts match; zero unnamed controls and zero images without alternative text; a keyboard-only run completes the primary task; contrast pairs pass; the tab order log matches visual order.
notes: Breakpoints copied from a framework default rarely match the original; measure where the layout actually changes.
Sideways scroll on phones usually comes from one fixed-width child; assert page width against viewport per width.
Accessibility regressions are measurable counts, so put them in the harness rather than a manual checklist.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/kinds/website.rs (page claims, landmark and a11y comparisons, sideways-scroll rule); AGENTS.md (accessibility rules)

title: Acceptance Self-Test Harness
description: 先写断言清单再改：通过、失败、未测量三种结论
prompt: Write the acceptance self-test harness before the last pass, so fixes are driven by measurement. Structure it as a flat list of claims, each one sentence, each judged by a check that returns passed, failed or unmeasured with a detail string. First build the harness: a script that builds the project, serves the output on loopback, captures each page at the configured widths, and writes a JSON report per round. Then add claims in four groups. Visual: per width likeness score plus page height delta. Structural: landmarks, heading text present, section order, missing parts. Behavioural: menus and modals open on click and on Enter, focus returns to the trigger, no console errors the original does not also log, no failing request the original does not also have. Content: no missing headings, no dropped words. Then add the rule that matters: a check that could not measure something reports unmeasured and blocks a pass, so silence is never rounded up to success. Acceptance self-tests: the harness reports each claim with its evidence, an overall score and an explicit unknowns list; two consecutive runs give the same result; a deliberately broken build fails the right claim and no other; the loop is capped at three rounds and stops when a round changes nothing.
notes: Never report a check that did not run as passed; the unmeasured list is the most useful part of the report.
Assert relations (inside, wider than, changed) rather than exact values you chose, or every cosmetic tweak breaks the suite.
Cap refinement rounds and stop on a round that changes nothing; otherwise a failing comparison loops forever.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + crates/ai/src/rebuild/check.rs (claims, similarity, unknowns); crates/engine/src/self_test.rs; docs/extending.md (a way to judge a build)

title: Screenshot Diff Verification Loop
description: 遮罩动态区做像素与结构双评分，逐档定位差异
prompt: Verify the replica with a screenshot diff that is honest about what it cannot see. Preparation: serve the build at the same viewport sizes as the reference, set the same device pixel ratio, wait for fonts and images to settle, disable smooth scrolling, and freeze or mask anything that changes by itself (carousels, video, clocks, live counters) by drawing opaque boxes over those regions in both images so they are excluded rather than scored. Compare each pair two ways: a layout score from coarse regional colour, asking whether every block is in the right place and size, and a perceptual score from structural similarity on brightness, asking whether the text and edges match. Report both, because layout alone flatters mostly empty pages. Crop both to the common height and state each page's real height, since a shorter build silently scores well. Tolerances: 24 per channel for pixels, and treat sub-3-channel colour differences as identical. Output per width the score, the height delta, the worst regions ranked, and the top differences as plain sentences: layout and section order first, then spacing, type sizes, colour, missing copy. Acceptance self-tests: the harness reproduces the reference capture with the same recipes; deleting one section drops the score by at least 10 points; the score improves after each fix round; every diff saves its mask image.
notes: Mask dynamic regions instead of averaging them; one carousel otherwise dominates the diff and hides real layout errors.
Score height delta alongside similarity; a build that stops early looks aligned but is missing a third of the page.
Compare at identical DPR and after fonts load, or antialiasing differences read as design differences.

title: Clone This Hero in Thirty Minutes
description: 五个计时阶段：取证、令牌、蓝图、实现、自测
prompt: Clone this hero in thirty minutes, working in five timed passes so scope cannot expand. Minutes 0 to 5, evidence: capture the hero at 1440, 1024 and 390 px plus its hover, focus, open and loading states; open each screenshot and write down only what you can see. Minutes 5 to 9, tokens: sample five colours, four type sizes with line-heights, the spacing ladder, two radii and the shadow; write tokens.css. Minutes 9 to 14, blueprint: one grid with named areas, the exact headline breaks, a control state table, and a mechanics sheet of numbers each with a source or an estimated mark. Minutes 14 to 24, craft: semantic markup, one component per grid area, tokens only, states through data attributes, entrance stagger under 600 ms on transform and opacity, one image with an explicit aspect ratio. Minutes 24 to 28, self-test: Tab through every control, check focus rings, pointer and keyboard parity, no sideways scroll at 390 px, no console errors, no layout shift; capture your build at the same three widths. Minutes 28 to 30, diff: compare pairs side by side, fix the single biggest difference, and write the remaining gap as a known limit. Done means all six: state parity, token purity, matching headline breaks, first-fold height within 24 px, no new console errors, and a written list of what is still unverified.
notes: The timebox is the technique: a hero that is 95 percent right in 30 minutes beats a perfect header with no page.
Stop at two failed attempts on one difference and record the limit instead of burning the polish pass.
Rebuild copy and imagery as your own; a visually identical clone with the original's brand assets is not shippable.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + README.md (Study, Build, Check, Ready); crates/ai/src/rebuild/brief.rs (how to work); crates/setup/src/skill.md (evidence-first method)

title: Control Size Scale
description: 把控件高度、字号、内边距与图标绑成一套尺寸令牌
prompt: Derive one control size scale and let every control on the page come from it. Pick four heights, 24, 32, 40 and 48 px, and bind each height to a label size, a side padding and an icon box so a row of mixed controls lines up without per-page fixes: 24 px for toolbar and table rows with 12 px padding and a 14 px icon, 32 px as the default with 13 px padding and a 16 px icon, 40 px for full-width fields and a screen's main switch, 48 px kept for the single primary action with 20 px padding and a 20 px icon. Declare them as control-sm, control-md, control-lg and control-xl, each exposing --control-height, --control-pad-x, --control-font and --control-icon, so a component reads one token and inherits all four values. Ban bare numbers in component CSS and enforce it with a test that walks component sources for px literals outside the token file; allow only computed sizes such as calc(var(--control-height) - 2px) for inner content. Render the scale as one page: each control at each size, in rest, hover, focus-visible, pressed and disabled, with its measured box printed beside it. Then verify the rule by swapping a medium button to large and confirming height, padding, label and icon move together and nothing else changes. Acceptance: two controls of the same size measure the same outer height within 1 px; no component file holds a literal height or padding; the label and focus ring stay optically centred at all four sizes; the rendered heights are exactly 24, 32, 40 and 48 px at 100 percent zoom.
notes: The failure mode is a one-off 36 px control that forces every neighbour to compensate; four sizes cover almost every real screen.
Give each size one job in the token file, or reviewers will pick by look and the scale decays within a sprint.
The upstream scale is documented by craft-anything under Apache-2.0; these four heights were chosen and measured for the web build.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (control sizes, rules); crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs (size tokens and the no-raw-numbers test)
