title: Type Scale and Leading System
description: 七级字号阶梯加统一行高比，规定每级用途与最大级数
prompt: Fix a seven-step type ramp and one leading ratio, then reject any text that is not on it. Choose the steps 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 20 and 26 px and give each a job in the token file: 11 and 12 for dense metadata, timestamps and captions, 13 for labels and list rows, 15 for body copy, 17 for a lead paragraph, 20 for card and section headings, 26 for the page title. State that a single screen may use at most four steps. Derive line height as 1.45 times the size for anything that wraps, and a fixed 1.2 for single-line labels, button text and headings; round both to whole pixels so glyphs keep sharp edges, and expose --text-n-size and --text-n-leading together. Set a measure of 62 to 70 characters by capping the lead at 34em and body at 38em, and write the rule that a line-height literal never appears outside the token file. Build a specimen page showing one paragraph at every step with its wrapped line count printed beside it, plus a long unbroken token, a 14-character compound and a string of digits to prove the wrap and the number spacing hold. Then set the same copy at 1440 and at 390 px. Acceptance: exactly seven sizes exist; no rendered text sits outside the ramp; each wrapped block measures within 1 px of 1.45 times its size; no line exceeds 76 characters; the specimen shows no clipped descender at any step.
notes: Seven steps is already generous; eight or more means nobody can name the difference between two of them.
Derive leading from the size instead of storing a per-component value, or headings and body drift apart on the next edit.
The 1.45 ratio follows the craft-anything scale (Apache-2.0); the web build fixes 1.2 for single lines, which desktop text did not need.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (the scale, rules on leading)
source.research: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (the scale, rules on leading)

title: Surface and Edge System
description: 只留五种表面与三态描边，让可点击区域自证可读
prompt: Choose the smallest set of surfaces the page actually needs, then give each pressable control one edge colour per pointer state. Keep five surfaces, canvas, card, field, hover and pressed, stepping luminance by about 4 percent per level so the ladder is visible at a glance without looking striped; the field step is a shade lighter than the card so anything to type in reads as something to use. Every control draws the same edge: 1 px card-border at rest, 1 px field-border under the pointer together with the lighter fill, accent at 2 px while pressed, open or typed in. Treat the rest edge as decoration at roughly 1.5 to 1 and make the interactive edge the measured one, at 3 to 1 against its own fill, because that is the state a person has to find. Write the rule that clickability is never signalled by a border alone: fill, edge and cursor move together. Build one page with every surface labelled, the same button repeated on each surface, and a swatch strip printing measured hex and contrast per pair, then repeat the page in the opposite theme. Acceptance: exactly five surface tokens exist; the pointer-state edge reaches 3 to 1 on every surface it appears on; luminance order stays strict in both themes; no component invents a sixth fill; a 4x crop of a control on a card shows a single clean edge.
notes: A 3:1 edge at rest makes every card look like a button; keep the rest edge soft and put the contrast budget into the hover state.
Test the edge against the fill it sits on, not against the page background, or controls on cards quietly drop below target.
Surfaces and edges are described in the craft-anything design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the percentages here were measured on the web build.

title: Focus Ring Spec
description: 一套焦点环：发丝描边加柔光晕，逐表面测对比度
prompt: Specify a single focus treatment and hold every control to it. Draw it in two parts: a 2 px hairline in the accent ink following the control's own radius, plus a 3 px halo outside it at about 35 percent alpha, so the ring reads at 1440 px and is never clipped by an overflow container. Fix the geometry: hairline inset 0, halo outside by 3 px, no layout growth, no offset drift on rounded corners, and a ring that stays whole when two controls sit 4 px apart. Set the target at 3 to 1 for the hairline against the surface directly outside the control, and list the surface pairs that fail, replacing the accent per surface rather than shipping a ring nobody can see. Differentiate the two families: buttons, toggles and links take the full ring on :focus-visible only, while text fields and selects show it on :focus and simultaneously switch their edge to the interactive colour, because a field is a place to type rather than something to press. Keep the ring visible through hover and active, and never ease it longer than 120 ms. Then audit by keyboard at both themes and at 200 percent zoom. Acceptance: Tab reaches every interactive element in visual order with a visible ring; no ring is clipped or shifts layout; measured contrast is at least 3 to 1 on all five surfaces in both themes; Enter and Space still activate while the ring shows; a pointer-only run leaves no ring behind.
notes: Outline with a positive offset is the one property that survives overflow hidden; a box-shadow ring disappears inside scroll containers.
Removing the ring and adding your own on hover is the usual regression: test with the keyboard, not the mouse.
The two-part hairline plus halo follows the craft-anything design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the pixel values were re-measured for a browser at 100 percent.

title: Component Need Map
description: 把页面需求逐条映射到组件，表格即开发顺序
prompt: Translate the page into a table of needs before choosing a single component. Read the reference screen and list every action and readout it carries, then write two columns, need and component, resolving each need to one entry of a fixed vocabulary: the one main action on a screen becomes a primary button at 40 or 48 px, any other action a secondary at 32 or 40, a quiet action that owns no box until hovered a ghost, anything that deletes or cannot be undone a filled danger button, one of a few choices a segmented control at 32 px with a sliding selection, one of many a dropdown whose rows are 32 px, a value to type a 40 px field with a real label, a status word a fully round pill, a name and its value a two-column stat row rather than a sentence, and nothing yet an empty state carrying one next action. Cap the plan at one primary per screen and one danger per destructive flow, and forbid a destructive control within 64 px of a primary one. Order the rows as the build order: shell, navigation, main action, fields, list and rows, status, empty and error. Each row names its states before it is coded, rest, hover, focus-visible, pressed, disabled, plus open or loading where they apply. Acceptance: every interactive element in the build maps to a row; no row goes unused; no screen shows two primary buttons; every row lists its states before implementation; the destructive distance rule holds; the table alone is enough for a second developer to start the build.
notes: The table is the deliverable: a need with no component is a missing design decision, and a component with no need is decoration.
Two primary buttons on one screen is the most common plan error and it survives every later polish pass.
Component vocabulary here follows craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the pixel sizes are this build's own measured values.

title: Message and Toast System
description: 提示卡分层：确认自散、错误常驻、单队列单归属
prompt: Design the message layer as one queue with one owner. Place it in a single fixed region, 24 px from the top and horizontally centred, stacked downward with 8 px gaps, above content and below any modal, so a message never appears in two corners at once. A message is a compact card with 12 px padding, a 6 px radius, a 4 px accent bar on its leading edge, a 15 px line and a 24 px close target. Bind lifetime to kind: a confirmation fades in over 120 ms, holds 4000 ms and leaves over 160 ms; a new confirmation replaces the one before it instead of stacking; errors and warnings never self-dismiss and stay until closed or resolved; progress and long-running status stay until their task ends. Let clicks pass through the card to the work underneath except on the close button, edit in place where a message carries a value, and never let the layer capture scroll or shift layout. Keep at most three visible, queue the rest and promote them as slots free. Give each message a status role, polite for confirmations and assertive for errors, plus a text label, so colour is never the only signal. Then fire five messages inside two seconds and dismiss one mid-fade. Acceptance: no two confirmations are visible together; errors survive 60 s untouched; the visible cap is three with the rest ordered; the layer adds zero layout shift; each message is announced exactly once.
notes: A message that covers the control the person just pressed reads as a failure of the app, not feedback; anchor it away from the working area.
Self-dismissing errors are the classic bug: a failure that vanishes in four seconds is a failure nobody can read or copy.
Queue rules mirror the message behaviour in craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the timings here were set for a browser, not a desktop window.

title: Empty and Loading States
description: 空白、加载、错误三态各配一种指示器与恢复路径
prompt: Give every list and panel three designed states and a rule for picking the indicator. Empty: a 20 px icon at 50 percent opacity, one 15 px line naming what is missing, one action that fixes it, and no illustration above 96 px. Loading: a determinate progress bar with a percentage when the wait is expected to pass one second and the total is known, an indeterminate 2 px bar when it is not, and a 16 px spinner only under one second; never an animated ellipsis, and never a skeleton built from animated gradients and blurs, because that is compositor work every frame for no information. Error: the same block shape as empty, the failure in one 15 px line, a retry action and a collapsible detail, and the retry keeps the person's filter values instead of resetting them. Reserve the block's height at 240 px and keep header and column widths identical across all three, so switching never nudges the page. Give each state one sentence for assistive technology, and pause any indicator animation while the tab is hidden. Then test a cold load, a load throttled to 300 ms latency and a forced network failure. Acceptance: all three states render inside the same 240 px block with no layout shift; no spinner is shown for a wait past one second; retry restores the previous query; each state is announced once; no indicator animates while the tab is hidden.
notes: A skeleton that does not match the final shape reads as a jump when content lands; reserve the real heights instead of drawing placeholder bars.
Replace framework defaults that repaint a spinner every frame with a CSS-driven indicator, or the idle state costs battery on every screen.
Nothing here needs a library; the behaviour mirrors the working and empty-state guidance in craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0).

title: Popup and Menu Behaviour
description: 下拉与菜单的开合、九行上限、宽度与焦点规则
prompt: Pin down how a dropdown opens, closes and behaves when the viewport is short. Open it with a 120 ms fade and no scale, rows already in place so the list never appears to grow; close in 90 ms and unmount only after the fade ends. Size the panel to its widest row plus 16 px of padding and never to full width, cap the height at nine 32 px rows, 288 px plus 8 px of padding, and scroll past that with a slim thumb. Place it 4 px below the trigger; when less than the panel height plus 12 px remains below, flip above and keep the same gap; when neither side fits, open at the larger side, scroll from the top and keep the trigger in view. On open, move focus to the selected row without scrolling it into the middle, let arrows traverse rows and wrap at the ends, send Home and End to the extremes, close on Escape and return focus to the trigger, and close on an outside pointer-down without swallowing that click. Mark the trigger with aria-expanded and aria-haspopup, give the active row aria-selected, and use real menu rows rather than restyled buttons. Then drive it with the keyboard in a 320 px tall window. Acceptance: measured fade times land within 10 ms of spec; exactly nine rows show before scrolling; panel width equals widest row plus 16 px; focus returns to the trigger after Escape and after an outside click; the panel opens fully inside the viewport at every tested height.
notes: Fading without a matching fade-out leaves the panel to vanish; finish the exit before unmount or the close reads as a glitch.
Width tracking the widest row is what stops a menu from being either cramped or absurdly wide when one label changes.
Popup fade and the nine-row cap come from craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the flip and focus rules are this build's addition for the web.

title: Wheel Step and Scrollbar Craft
description: 一格滚轮走多远、缓动多久、滑块多粗与对比度
prompt: Build the scrolling feel from numbers rather than taste. Fix one wheel notch at 100 px of travel on the page and ease to it over 180 ms on a decelerating curve, so a single notch lands exactly and a second notch inside that window adds to the target instead of restarting the curve; normalize raw deltas across mouse and trackpad, clamp any single event to 120 px, and leave Page Down at one viewport height minus 64 px of overlap so a line of context survives. Use the same 100 px step and the same easing inside short scroll containers, so a panel and the page do not feel like two different products. Draw a scrollbar with no visible track: a 6 px thumb whose colour holds 3 to 1 against every surface it crosses, thickening to 10 px under the pointer with a 120 ms transition on width and colour, and appearing only after 500 ms of scroll activity so it is not a permanent stripe. Position it as an overlay so it never changes layout width, and never hide the native bar where a keyboard or assistive path still needs a target. Then drive it with a scripted wheel sequence and a trackpad. Acceptance: one notch settles within 2 px of 100 px of travel; two fast notches accumulate without restarting; the thumb holds 3 to 1 on the darkest and the lightest surface; hover thickening shifts no content; no wheel input ever scrolls the page sideways.
notes: A theme that paints the thumb and the track with the same token makes the bar invisible except on hover; check both in both themes and measure, not by eye.
Smooth scrolling that re-targets on every wheel event fights the person scrolling; accumulate into one target instead.
The 100-point wheel step and the slim thickening thumb follow craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the pixel and millisecond values here were tuned in a browser.

title: Theme Parity Snapshot
description: 双主题同场景快照与逐对对比度，禁止硬编码颜色
prompt: Build every screen from tokens and prove both themes in one run. Define a semantic layer instead of two palettes: canvas, card, field, hover, pressed, text, muted, accent, danger and edge, each resolving through a light set and a dark set, and make a check fail the build when a component contains a hex value or a raw rgba. Then write a snapshot script that renders each scene at 1440 by 900 in light and dark, waits for document.fonts.ready plus 300 ms of quiet, and writes both captures beside a side-by-side sheet per scene. For every surface pair, compute text contrast and interactive-edge contrast in each theme and print the ratios in the report, targeting 4.5 to 1 for body text and 3 to 1 for large text and control edges; treat a pair that passes in only one theme as a failure rather than a footnote. Diff the two captures structurally to catch a component that kept a light-only shadow, a white overlay or an rgba border, since those survive a token audit and still break dark. Re-run everything from a cold load and then from a live toggle without reload. Acceptance: the token check reports zero raw colours in components; every scene has both captures; no contrast pair passes in one theme and fails in the other; the toggle run matches the cold load within 2 per channel; the report names any pair it could not measure.
notes: A snapshot that only renders the default theme ships half the product; run both in the same pass or the second one never happens.
Contrast that passes in dark and fails in light is the usual asymmetry, because accent inks are chosen against a dark canvas.
Token layering and the snapshot idea come from craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the capture steps here are a browser harness, not a desktop example binary.

title: Form Field Architecture
description: 字段拆成标签、控件、提示、错误、成功五部分
prompt: Assemble a field from named parts and fix where each one sits. The parts are label at 13 px, 4 px above the control, always visible and never replaced by a placeholder; control at 40 px with 12 px side padding, a 6 px radius and 15 px text; hint at 12 px muted, 4 px below the control; error at 12 px in the danger ink with a 14 px icon, taking the hint's slot; and success in the same slot, accent ink, one word. Reserve 18 px under every field for whichever of hint, error or success is showing, so validation never moves the form. Combine states on purpose: focus draws the accent edge plus the halo and keeps the error text visible when the value is still invalid, while error without focus holds a 2 px danger edge. Validate on blur for the first attempt and on input only after the first failure, and never disable the submit button as a substitute for explaining what is wrong. Handle autofill by repainting the browser's autofill fill to the field colour so contrast survives, and long values by ellipsis in read mode with the full value in edit mode. Then test an 80-character value, a paste, an autofilled email and a screen reader pass. Acceptance: all five parts exist for every field; error and success swap with zero layout shift; no invalid state relies on colour alone; autofill keeps field contrast above 4.5 to 1; a keyboard-only submit reaches every hint and error through aria-describedby.
notes: Reserved space is the whole trick: fields that grow when an error appears make the submit button move under the cursor.
A disabled submit button hides the failure and gives nobody a way to ask what is missing; keep it enabled and explain.
The field vocabulary follows craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the validation timing and autofill handling were chosen for browsers.

title: Navigation Breakpoints
description: 按内容宽度定位导航折叠点，四档截图证明
prompt: Decide from measurement where horizontal navigation stops fitting and becomes a menu button. Capture the reference at 1280, 1024, 768 and 390 px and record, per width, the header height, the number of visible links, which actions stay outside the menu, and whether the wordmark shrinks or drops to a mark. Choose the threshold from content rather than habit: convert when the measured row would exceed its container minus 24 px of breathing room, which for six realistic labels lands near 820 px, and write that number down as a token instead of adopting a framework step. Decide what moves and in what order: secondary utilities collapse first, primary destinations go into the menu, and the one main action stays visible as a 40 px icon button with an accessible name, never as a truncated word. Keep the header at 64 px in both modes so the first band of content never jumps, animate the panel in over 180 ms from the menu button's edge, trap focus inside while it is open, return focus on close, close on Escape and on route change, and mark the button with aria-expanded. Then prove the whole thing with four captures and a keyboard run. Acceptance: captures exist at all four widths; no width shows a wrapped or clipped nav row; header height is identical in both modes; the menu opens and closes by keyboard alone; every destination reachable at 1280 px is present in the mobile menu.
notes: The breakpoint is a property of the labels, not of the design system; six long words break a nav at a width where six short ones still fit.
A hamburger that opens a panel without trapping focus leaves the keyboard user behind it, which is worse than no menu at all.
Window and component thinking here follows craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the widths are this build's measured values.

source.ref: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (window, components); crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs (control composition and header behaviour)
source.research: storytold/craft-anything + docs/design-system.md (window, components); crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs (control composition and header behaviour)

title: Icon Size System
description: 图标六档尺寸与描边权重，随控件尺寸成对使用
prompt: Set an icon scale that pairs with the control sizes and refuse to mix weights. Use six sizes, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24 and 32 px, and bind each to its job: 12 for inline text and dense table marks, 14 for small toolbar buttons and list rows, 16 for default buttons, chevrons and field affordances, 20 for large controls and the primary action, 24 for navigation and standalone icon buttons, 32 for empty states and page headers. Draw every glyph on one 24-unit grid with a 1.5-unit stroke at 20 and 24 px and 1.25 units at 12 to 16 px, so optical weight stays constant as the size changes instead of thin icons turning to mush. Align to whole pixels, correct optical centring by 0.5 px where a shape is asymmetric, and cap one view at two sizes. Write which sizes may appear in which context in the token file, name each icon-only button for assistive technology, and give every icon a 44 px hit area even at 16 px of drawing. Then audit one full screen icon by icon against the scale and against the text beside it, at both themes. Acceptance: only the six sizes exist; stroke widths follow the size rule; every icon centres on its label's optical middle within 1 px; no view uses more than two sizes; every icon-only button carries an accessible name; a 4x crop shows nothing drawn on a half pixel.
notes: Mixed weights are the fastest way to make a clean layout read as assembled; one grid and two stroke widths fix more than redrawing.
Small icons need a hit area of their own, or a 12 px glyph becomes an unclickable target on a phone.
The icon ladder and control pairing follow craft-anything's design-system notes (Apache-2.0); the stroke units here were chosen for browser rendering.

title: Pricing Table Rebuild
description: 套餐卡、对比表与切换不跳动的重建
prompt: Rebuild a pricing section as three measured parts: plan cards, a comparison grid, and a billing toggle. Start with the cards. Record each plan's slots (name, price, unit, one-line claim, four to six feature rows, action label), the inner padding, the gap between cards, and how the recommended plan differs: an accent border at 1 px, a label at 12 px above the name, an 8 px lift that changes no column width. Use one radius family, 8 px on cards, 6 px on the toggle and buttons, 4 px on feature rows. Then the toggle: two labels, a slider that moves in 180 ms on the standard ease, and a price swap that changes digits only, so nothing above or below the row moves; reserve the widest value with tabular figures and a min-width on the price element. Then the comparison grid: eight rows maximum, feature column at 40 percent, one column per plan, row separators at 12 percent alpha, sticky row labels, and a collapse rule at 640 px that keeps the feature name, the recommended plan, and a disclosure per row. Acceptance: toggling at 1440, 1024 and 390 px moves no element by more than 1 px; the recommended card is unique and labelled in markup, not by colour alone; the grid never scrolls sideways at 390 px; every price cell uses tabular figures; keyboard focus reaches the toggle and every action with a 3 px halo.
notes: The price swap is where this section fails: give the price element a fixed min-width and tabular figures, or every toggle press drags the layout a few pixels sideways.
Reserve about 12 px of extra width per digit; a reservation sized to this month's numbers breaks when annual pricing needs five digits.
Mark the recommended plan once in markup rather than painting it, so both the stylesheet and a screen reader agree on which one it is.

title: Mega Footer Craft
description: 大页脚列数、密度与法务信息的排版规则
prompt: Lay out a large footer as a fixed column grammar rather than a sitemap dump. Cap it at five columns plus a brand block: brand column 280 px with wordmark, one sentence and two social links; then four link columns, each with a heading at 13 px and no more than six links, separated by 32 px of horizontal space. Link text sits at 14 px with a 1.45 line height and 8 px of vertical rhythm; hover changes colour only, in 120 ms, and never underlines, because an underline on a 14 px footer link reflows the line. Give legal and locale their own row: language selector, region, privacy, terms, and a copyright line, all reachable by keyboard, separated from the columns by a hairline at 8 percent alpha. Build with CSS grid, logical properties, and tokens for every gap and colour. The rule that keeps a footer readable: it carries every destination a person needs at the end of a page, not every page the site owns; when a column would need a seventh link, that content belongs in a hub page, not a longer column. Acceptance: at 1440 px the footer is at most 420 px tall; at 390 px the columns stack on a 24 px rhythm and stay under 720 px; link contrast is at least 4.5 to 1 on the footer surface; no label wraps to a third line; tabbing reaches every link in visual order; the total link count stays at or under 30.
notes: Footers grow by accretion: each team adds one link and a year later a column has nineteen. Enforce the six-link cap inside the component, not in review comments.
Keep the legal row quiet but not tiny; 12 px is the floor and it still has to reach 7 to 1 against the footer surface.
Measure footer height at 1440 and 390 px after every addition; growth nobody feels is what makes the end of a page look cheap.

title: Content Model Before Layout
description: 先定文案槽位与长度上限，再写布局
prompt: Write the content model before any layout exists, so real copy drives the grid instead of placeholder text. Produce one table, one row per string and asset the section needs: key, role, English text, measured character count, maximum allowed characters, minimum, may wrap, is editable, and which element renders it. Cover headline, eyebrow, subhead, action labels, feature titles, feature bodies, captions, table headers, empty copy, error copy, alt text and the logo slot. Take the English length by counting characters, not words, and set the maximum at 130 percent of it rounded up to the nearest 5. Anything under 40 characters must not wrap; body copy wraps between 62 and 68 characters per line. Then write the constraints that follow from the numbers: the headline block holds a fixed two-line height so a longer string pushes nothing below it, card titles clamp at three lines, buttons take a 40 px height with 16 px side padding and truncate only past their own maximum. Add an overflow fixture per key: the longest allowed string, one string with an emoji, and one unbroken 40-character word. Acceptance: every visible string traces to a table row; injecting each overflow fixture changes no pixel outside its own block; a scan finds no key over its maximum; a second developer rebuilds the section from the table without reopening the reference.
notes: Designing against lorem ipsum hides the failure: the real headline arrives, the grid moves, and the rebuild stops matching the reference.
Set the maximum from the measurement rather than from a round number you like; round numbers are what break the first translation.
An unbroken 40-character word is the fixture nobody writes and every overflow test needs.

title: Motion Tier Budget
description: 把动效分四档，各给时长、缓动与频次预算
prompt: Split every animation into four tiers and give each one a number before writing a single transition. Tier zero, instant feedback: 0 to 90 ms, colour and shadow only, no easing token, unlimited count, because a press must feel immediate. Tier one, transition: 120 to 180 ms on the standard ease for hover, focus and toggle moves. Tier two, entrance: 220 to 320 ms on a decelerate curve, a 16 px rise, 40 to 60 ms of stagger between siblings, and a cap of six items so the last one lands under 620 ms. Tier three, ambient: 6 to 12 s loops, two per viewport at most, transform only. Exits run at 65 to 80 percent of their matching entrance. Then set the frequency budget, which is the part that actually changes how a page reads: a control may animate two properties per state change, a section may run one entrance per load, and nothing in tiers two or three may animate while scrolling unless it is a scroll-linked reveal with a 0.25 progress threshold and a once-only latch. Record every entry in a motion manifest: tier, duration, easing, property, element, trigger and count cap. Acceptance: a timeline dump matches each manifest duration within 20 percent; no entry animates width, height, top or left; with reduced motion every entrance collapses to opacity at 120 ms and every loop stops; the manifest lists fewer than 24 entries for the whole page.
notes: Tier inflation is the usual failure: when hover, toolbar, badge and marquee all animate, nothing on the page reads as important.
Ambient loops cost battery on phones, so two per viewport at 6 to 12 s is a budget rather than a preference.
An exit shorter than its entrance is what makes an interface feel quick; reuse the entrance duration for the way out and it reads sluggish.

title: State Coverage Matrix
description: 部件乘七种状态的覆盖矩阵与缺口清单
prompt: Build a state coverage matrix before styling anything, so the missing cells become the plan. Put parts down the left and states across the top, one cell per pair, each cell marked built, borrowed or missing. List the parts from the reference section: inline link, icon button, primary action, secondary action, segmented control, dropdown, text field, checkbox, card, tab, accordion row, carousel control, toast and one media hover. Across the top put seven states: rest, hover, focus-visible, active or open, disabled, loading, error. Fill what exists, then mark the remainder missing and count them; that number is the schedule, not an opinion. Write each cell's visible difference in one clause, for example hover on the secondary action raises its surface one step and moves nothing, while focus draws a 1 px hairline in the accent ink plus a 3 px halo. Build in dependency order: surfaces first, then hover and focus, then active and open, then disabled, then loading and error, since loading needs a reserved layout or the page jumps the moment a spinner appears. Acceptance: every part has all seven states either built or deferred with a written reason; a scripted pass sets each state by attribute and screenshots it; only open and error change layout height, each by a recorded amount; the matrix ends with zero unexplained empty cells.
notes: An empty state cell is not cosmetic; loading without a reserved layout produces the one shift a whole page gets judged on.
Seven states across fourteen parts is 98 cells, so expect the missing count to be honest rather than small.
Mark a deferred state with its reason; a blank cell cannot be told apart from an oversight at handoff.

title: Validation Message System
description: 校验时机、摆放位置与读屏播报的规则
prompt: Write the validation system before writing the form, because the timing decides whether the form feels calm or abusive. Rules first: validate on blur and on submit, never on keystroke, except a confirmation field, which may check per keystroke after its first submit failure. Clear an error the moment the field becomes valid on blur, not while typing. Give each message a rule id, a field, a trigger, the condition, the text and a severity. Then placement: reserve a 20 px message row under every field at all times so showing an error moves nothing; the message sits 6 px below the field, renders at 12 px, and carries a non-colour cue, an icon plus the word that failed, because colour alone is invisible to part of the audience. Then announcement: mark the field invalid, point it at its message with a described-by relation, move focus to the first invalid field on submit, and send one summary through a polite live region, once per submit rather than once per field. Error text says what to do in under 60 characters, in sentence case, without blame. Acceptance: submitting an empty form moves no element and announces a single summary; each message clears on its stated trigger; the reserved row keeps the submit button at the same y position with zero and with five errors; the announced output names field and message; error text reaches 4.5 to 1 and the invalid border 3 to 1.
notes: Validating on keystroke punishes typing: the error flickers while a correct value is half entered, and people stop trusting the form.
The reserved message row is what keeps the submit button still; without it a five-error submit shifts the whole form.
Test with a screen reader, not only the attribute: the invalid flag plus the described-by relation is what announces field and message together.

title: Waitlist and Onboarding Flow
description: 等候名单与引导流程：步骤、出错回复与终态
prompt: Lay out the waitlist or onboarding flow as numbered steps with exactly one action each. Define the steps first: entry with an email field, confirmation that the address was accepted, a profile step with two fields at most, and a done state that says what happens next and when. Each step carries a title at 18 px, one sentence of context, a single primary action at 40 px height, a back affordance, and a progress signal in text plus three 4 px bars, never an indefinite spinner. Write recovery for every failure before drawing the success path: invalid address, already subscribed, rate limited, network failure, expired token. Each gets its own message, one retry path and a support link, and no failure may leave the person on an unchanged screen. The end state is explicit: a dashboard link or a dated promise, never an empty success page with a checkmark. Cap the flow at four steps and two fields per step, and make each step fit one viewport at 390 px with its action visible without scrolling. Keep the whole flow on one route so a reload resumes at the current step rather than resetting. Acceptance: every step fits 390x844 with its action visible; Tab reaches action, back and retry in order; a forced network failure shows a retry that completes on the second attempt; no state lasts past 800 ms without a visible progress signal; a scripted run reaches the end state for success and for each failure.
notes: The spinner that never ends comes from treating a network failure as a state instead of a branch; every request needs a terminal state.
Four steps and two fields is the ceiling before completion drops, and that is measured on a phone where the keyboard covers half the viewport.
A success screen with no next action leaves people unsure it worked; name the next step and its date.

title: Data Table Density
description: 按类型对齐的密集数据表与手机卡片化
prompt: Rebuild a dense data table from its type ramp instead of from a comfortable default. Derive the row height: body text at 14 px with a 1.45 line height gives 20 px of text, plus 12 px top and bottom, so the compact row is 44 px; set a roomy row at 56 px and switch between them with one density token rather than a class per table. Align by data type: text left, numbers and currency right with tabular figures, dates right, status pills left, row actions right and never in the first column. Keep the header sticky with a 1 px separator and a surface one step lighter; choose separators or zebra striping, not both, and if zebra, cap the alternating fill at 4 percent alpha so scanning still works. Size numeric columns from the widest value, not from the header text, and let the flexible text column absorb the remaining width. Then the phone rule: below 768 px the table becomes cards, one card per row with a label and value pair per cell, secondary cells behind a disclosure, and the primary identifier as the card title. Acceptance: row height matches the density token at both settings; the header stays visible after scrolling 600 px; numeric columns stay right aligned with tabular figures at every width; no header wraps to two lines at 1440 px; the 390 px card view keeps every primary value; no tested width scrolls horizontally.
notes: Comfortable defaults turn a data table into a scrolling page; derive the row height once and density becomes a token instead of an argument.
Zebra above roughly 5 percent alpha fights the separators and makes the table read as a spreadsheet export.
Numbers need tabular figures or the columns visibly jitter whenever values change between renders.

title: Card Nesting and Radius Rules
description: 卡片的圆角家族、嵌套深度与内边距规则
prompt: Fix card nesting with three rules a reviewer can verify in one glance. Rule one, one radius family: outer containers 8 px, cards inside them 6 px, controls inside those 4 px, pills fully round, and no two radii at the same depth. Rule two, inset by exactly one spacing step, 8 or 12 px, and shift the inner surface one step in luminance rather than using both a lighter fill and a border. Rule three, at most two visible borders along any line from page edge to text: a bordered card inside a bordered card is exactly the failure this prevents. Depth comes from one light model: at rest a shadow of y 1 px, blur 2 px, alpha 12 percent; for the single floating element per view, y 8 px, blur 24 px, alpha 18 percent. Remove shadows from anything that already has a border, and never fake elevation with a border alone. Then audit by counting: for each card record depth level, radius, fill, border, shadow and inner padding, and read the table top to bottom. Acceptance: nothing sits at depth three or deeper without a written reason; a 4x corner crop shows no double outline; every nested padding value comes from the 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 ladder; text contrast holds at 4.5 to 1 at every nesting level; shadow offsets are identical on every surface.
notes: Nested borders multiply: a card inside a card with two outlines and an inset shadow reads as three boxes around one sentence.
Depth without direction looks like a bug, so pick one light source and keep every shadow offset identical.
A shadow inside a bordered card is the cheapest way to make a surface look muddy on a dark canvas.

title: Contrast Ladder Audit
description: 三档对比度审计，失败配对直接给替换令牌
prompt: Audit contrast as three ladders and report replacements rather than warnings. Ladder one, non-text at 3 to 1: field borders under the pointer, focus halos, icons that carry meaning, chart strokes, toggle tracks, scrollbar thumbs. Ladder two, body text at 4.5 to 1: paragraph copy, labels, table cells, and button text in every state including hover and disabled. Ladder three, small print at 7 to 1: anything at 12 px or below, captions, legal lines, timestamps, and text over imagery. Collect the pairs the page actually renders from computed styles, not from a palette file, and include pairs that only exist in hover, focus, disabled, error and glass-over-media states, since those are what an audit normally misses. Compute each ratio, then for every failure write one line: element, foreground, background, measured ratio, required ratio, and the nearest passing token already on the scale with its ratio. Change tokens rather than components, so one token fix closes several pairs. Run the whole audit in both themes and report them side by side. Acceptance: every failing pair names a replacement token and its ratio; no replacement creates a pair below its own threshold; a rerun after the fixes reports zero failures in both themes; text over media is measured against its worst-case scrim; disabled controls are listed separately instead of being silently exempted.
notes: Reporting low contrast without a replacement token makes the audit something a team redoes instead of fixes.
The pairs that only exist in hover, disabled and glass states are the ones audits miss, so read rendered styles rather than the palette.
Disabled text is exempt from the threshold in the guidelines and still has to be legible, so report it as its own line.

title: RTL and Bidi Parity
description: 从逻辑属性做镜像，数字与图标各守其位
prompt: Make one layout render in both directions, driven by logical properties rather than a second stylesheet. Start with the mirror pass: replace margin-left and margin-right with margin-inline, padding with padding-inline, left and right with inset-inline, and border sides with border-inline, then set direction on the document and confirm the page mirrors with no physical property left in a grep of the stylesheet. Next, the elements that must not mirror: brand marks, media play controls, progress direction, chart axes that carry time, code blocks, and direction-encoding icons such as a back arrow, which flips only when it means navigation and never when it means playback. Numbers, prices, phone numbers and identifiers stay left-to-right inside right-to-left text: wrap each in an isolation span with its own direction so trailing punctuation cannot jump to the wrong end. Then spacing and type: mirror asymmetric padding, keep paragraph line height at 1.45 of the size, and re-check the ramp, because ascenders and descenders in Arabic and Hebrew push the line box taller than the Latin sample did. Acceptance: a screenshot pair in both directions overlays within 2 px after mirroring; the grep finds no physical margin, padding or inset property; numbers keep the same digit order in both directions; the five direction-sensitive icons behave as listed; and at 390 px text overflows no container in either direction.
notes: Mirroring by hand with left and right leaves a stylesheet that works in one direction and bends silently in the other.
Direction-sensitive icons are the usual regression: a back arrow has to flip, a play triangle must not.
Line boxes grow in Arabic and Hebrew, so re-check the type ramp instead of trusting a mirrored screenshot.

title: Localisation String Budget
description: 翻译前先给每个字符串定长度上限与伸缩位
prompt: Budget strings before translating, or the layout breaks in the second language and nobody knows which element to change. Build a table with one row per key: namespace, English text, character count, expansion factor, allowed length, may wrap, single line, and the element that renders it. Assume 30 percent expansion for short labels and 35 percent for compounding languages, then set allowed lengths from measurement rather than taste: the primary action stays on one line and may not exceed 24 characters at 14 px inside its 40 px height; navigation items cap at 18; card titles clamp at two lines; body copy wraps freely between 45 and 70 characters. Mark which element flexes for each key: the button grows to 200 px before its label truncates, the segmented control divides its container instead of sizing to text, the headline block keeps a two-line height. Then test with three pseudo-locales generated from the source strings, a 130 percent longer one, an accented one, and a right-to-left one, and render every one at 390, 1024 and 1440 px. Acceptance: every key has a row with a measured English length; the longer pseudo-locale produces zero truncation outside keys marked truncatable; the action button stays 40 px tall in all three; no string overflows its container at 390 px; a scan shows every visible string resolved from the table with no literal text left in components.
notes: Translating before budgeting means the second language finds every layout that sized itself to English.
Pseudo-locales catch more than a real translation, because you choose the length and can re-run the check in seconds.
Reserve the expansion on the control rather than the page: a button growing to 200 px is cheaper than a container that reflows.

title: Design Handoff Scorecard
description: 一分钟可核的交付记分卡与未验证清单
prompt: Close the rebuild with a scorecard a reviewer can check in one minute. Seven rows, each a number or a yes, each paired with the command that produced it. Token purity: count hex colours and raw pixel values outside the token file, target zero. State coverage: built states over required states per part, target all seven. Themes: both rendered and diffed, with only documented differences allowed. Contrast: measured pairs over pairs below threshold, target zero below. Responsive parity: widths tested and page width against viewport at each, target no sideways scroll. Motion budget: manifest entries and the longest entrance in milliseconds, target under 620. Unverified items: an explicit numbered list that may not be empty unless the first six rows are clean. Add the rule that gives the scorecard its value: a check that could not measure something reports unmeasured and blocks its row, so silence is never rounded up into a green cell. Finish with the date, the widths and browsers used, and the one known gap the team consciously accepts, because a scorecard with no accepted gap is a scorecard nobody read. Acceptance: the scorecard fits one screen and every row cites its evidence; re-running the listed commands reproduces each number within rounding; a deliberately broken token fails exactly the token row; no row reads passed without a measurement behind it.
notes: A scorecard that reports only passes is decoration; the unverified list is what a reviewer should read first.
Every row needs the command that produced it, or the next person re-derives the numbers by hand and skips half of them.
Unmeasured is not a soft pass; it blocks its row until something measures it.

title: Liquid Chrome Raymarch Hero
description: 光线步进的液态铬金属英雄区，环境反射流动，鼠标推挤变形。
prompt: Build a full-viewport hero on a near-black #05060b canvas with an oversized chrome liquid-metal form breathing in the center, overlaid by a left-aligned headline in a tight sans at clamp(2.4rem, 6vw, 5.5rem) and one pill CTA. Render the metal with Three.js: a full-screen quad using a ShaderMaterial that raymarches an SDF built from 3-4 smoothly blended spheres plus sin-based noise displacement, 64-96 march steps, normals from the SDF gradient, and a procedural studio environment (two area-light gradients plus a horizon band) sampled by the reflection vector, with a Fresnel rim tinted #4d5bff. Animate the noise time at 0.25 units per second and ease a pointer-driven bulge with a 0.06 lerp. Cap devicePixelRatio at 1.5, render at half resolution on mobile, and pause the rAF loop when the canvas is offscreen or the tab is hidden. Under prefers-reduced-motion render one static frame and skip pointer influence. Keep the copy above the canvas at 0.92 opacity with a 24px vignette blur at the edges. Acceptance: 60fps on a 2021 laptop GPU at 1440x900, no popping on resize (debounce the resize uniform 150ms), the headline stays legible over the brightest highlight via a subtle text-shadow, and there is zero layout shift before the canvas mounts.
notes: Shader is the main GPU cost: cap DPR, pause rAF offscreen, and never render the full DPR on phones.
Reduced motion gets a single static frame so the hero still reads as premium without animation.
Original GLSL; three.js is MIT and the raymarching approach follows Codrops (MIT demo). Do not paste Codrops or Shadertoy shader source verbatim; Shadertoy defaults to CC BY-NC-SA.

title: Grainy Gradient Mesh Backdrop
description: 多层柔和渐变光斑叠加胶片噪点并缓慢漂移的深色背景。
prompt: Create a full-bleed background section: four soft radial blobs (#ff5f7a, #7b61ff, #f2ff8a, #2dd4bf) at 1100-1400px diameter, filter blur(70px), opacity 0.55-0.8, distributed partly off-canvas on a #0a0912 base, morphing with 26s, 34s and 41s ease-in-out infinite alternate keyframes that move each blob 6-10% and scale 0.92-1.08. Add film grain as one inline SVG filter: feTurbulence type=fractalNoise, baseFrequency 0.78, numOctaves 3, stitchTiles=stitch, painted on a full-cover rect, composited with mix-blend-mode overlay at opacity 0.11 on an ::after layer; add a second blurred coarse copy at opacity 0.05 for dust. Keep all motion on transform and opacity only. Foreground: a centered two-line display headline at clamp(2.5rem, 5vw, 5rem) plus an 18px subline at 78% width, over a 40% black radial scrim so text keeps at least 7:1 contrast above the brightest blob. Responsive: below 768px use two blobs and drop the second grain layer. Reduced motion: freeze all drift keyframes and keep grain static. Acceptance: grain tiles with no visible seams at 1440x900, under 2ms of extra paint time versus a flat background, grain never intercepts pointer events, and the SVG filter is defined once and reused by reference.
notes: One tiled grain filter keeps paint cost flat regardless of viewport size; do not animate the filter itself.
Blobs are transform/opacity only, and a scrim protects headline contrast when a bright blob drifts behind it.
feTurbulence is a W3C/SVG platform primitive (no license); the composition is original. React Bits Grainient is a MIT + Commons Clause reference only.

title: Variable-Font Kinetic Headline
description: 大标题字重随光标距离连续变化，配合错峰入场的动态排版英雄区。
prompt: Design a type-only hero: a #0b0b0c stage with a left-aligned three-line headline in a variable sans (Inter Variable or Space Grotesk, SIL OFL) at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 8.5rem), line-height 0.9, letter-spacing -0.03em, color #f4f2ec, with one accent word in #ff4d1c. Split the headline into per-character spans, keep the full string in an aria-label on the parent and set the spans aria-hidden. On pointer move, measure each glyph's distance to the cursor; inside a 180px radius map distance through smoothstep to font-variation-settings wght 420-900 and letter-spacing 0-0.02em. Smooth each glyph with a spring (stiffness 180, damping 22) integrated once per rAF frame, never per event. Entrance: per-glyph opacity 0-1 and translateY 24px-0 over 520ms with cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) and 18ms stagger. Add a 1px horizontal rule plus a mono eyebrow at 0.18em tracking, and a small caption bottom-right. Responsive: shrink the radius to 120px under 900px, clamp spring delta time to 34ms, and gate the effect behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Reduced motion: all glyphs settle at wght 620, no entrance translate, cursor mapping off. Acceptance: no reflow because variation axes change weight without swapping fonts, 60fps with 40 glyphs, text stays selectable, and the layout matches a screenshot at 1280x800 and 390x844.
notes: Only use OFL/Apache variable fonts and verify the actual wght axis range, or the effect collapses to a binary bold.
One rAF loop drives every glyph spring; adding a listener per character is the usual performance failure here.
Pattern follows React Bits Variable Proximity (MIT + Commons Clause, attribution required); this prompt text is original.

title: Decrypt Scramble Microcopy
description: 字符先随机跳动再逐字锁定为真文，黑客风但克制的滚动与悬停微交互。
prompt: Build a reusable scramble-reveal component. Given a target string, render it uppercase in a monospace face at 0.08em tracking, color #e6ffe6 on #0a0a0a, and reserve the final width so nothing reflows. Trigger on first entry into view (IntersectionObserver, threshold 0.4) and on hover. Run a 950ms reveal where every character first shows a random glyph from ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#$%& and locks to the real character when a left-to-right front passes its index. Tick roughly 32ms with requestAnimationFrame, but derive progress from elapsed time so slow frames do not stretch the duration; stagger 12ms between neighbours and keep every fourth space permanent. Hover re-run: scramble only the hovered word for 450ms, never the whole line. Mark the animated span aria-hidden, expose the true string in aria-label, and respect prefers-reduced-motion by painting the final string immediately. Add a 1px #39ff14 underline that draws in over 300ms after the reveal, and a small mono label such as 0x1F above the block. Acceptance: final state is exactly the target string with no width jump because width is measured once, CPU stays under 3% when idle, scroll-back re-triggers at most once per element, and screen readers announce the label once with no glyph noise.
notes: Time-based progress keeps the 950ms duration honest on 60Hz, 120Hz and throttled devices.
aria-label carries the real text while the animated span is hidden from assistive tech; re-runs are capped.
Pattern follows React Bits Decrypted Text (MIT + Commons Clause, attribution required); implementation is original.

title: Magnetic Spring Buttons

title: Vertical-Scroll Horizontal Gallery
description: 纵向滚动驱动横向画廊，粘性视口、弹簧跟手与逐卡视差。

title: WebGL Image Distortion on Hover
description: 悬停图片时产生 RGB 分离、噪声波纹与轻微形变的 WebGL 画廊。

title: Lenis Smooth-Scroll Choreography
description: Lenis 惯性平滑滚动，用滚动速度驱动倾斜与视差，统一整页节奏。

title: Split-Flap Text Board

title: Odometer Counter Roll
description: 里程表式数字滚动，逐位进位且宽度不抖
prompt: Build a counter that rolls like a mechanical odometer rather than tweening a formatted string. Each digit is a 0.62em by 1em window with overflow hidden; inside sits a vertical strip of 0-9 stacked at exactly 1em line-height, translated by minus digitIndex times 1em. Set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums and verify it by rendering 1111 next to 8888 at the same size — if the columns differ by a pixel the axis is missing and every tick will jitter. Pin the counter to a min-width computed once from the widest value it will ever show, and keep the digit windows on integer pixel positions. On a value change animate only the strips that actually moved: translateY from the old index to the new over 620ms with cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), and let carries run leftward so 199 to 200 rolls the ones, tens and hundreds strips with a 70ms offset per column to the right. Drive all strips from one requestAnimationFrame loop and one shared progress value, so a value bump costs a single frame budget no matter how many digits move; snap the final translateY to an exact multiple of 1em to avoid subpixel haze. Separate thousands with a comma in #2a2f3a at 0.9 opacity. Reduced motion: set the strips directly with no transition, same final value and same accessible text. Acceptance: columns never shift a subpixel mid-tween, tabular-nums is proven by the 1111 and 8888 comparison, exactly one rAF loop runs per counter, and the live region announces the settled value once instead of announcing every frame.

One shared driver is the budget promise: per-digit tweens multiply frame cost by the digit count for no visual gain.

title: SVG Path Draw Diagram
description: 线图随滚动逐条描边，节点标签在边完成后出现
prompt: Animate a three-node architecture diagram so its edges draw themselves as the reader scrolls. Author one inline SVG with a viewBox of 800x420, six paths on a 1.5px #8ea2ff stroke with round caps on a #0b0d12 panel, node circles at r=7 in #e8ecf7, and real <text> labels at 12px with 0.02em tracking. Stagger the six edges 90ms apart so the figure reads as a sequence rather than a pulse, and give each edge a slight curvature via a quadratic control point offset 18px from the straight line. A label fades from opacity 0 and translateY 6px to its resting position only after its incoming edge reaches dashoffset 0, with a 180ms delay and a 300ms ease-out; a diagonal connector between nodes must not draw before its source node is labelled. Recompute lengths on resize inside a 100ms debounce, and honour vertical writing by redrawing in DOM order. Server-rendered and printed output ships with dashoffset 0 so crawlers, print and no-JS readers receive the complete figure. Reduced motion: full stroke immediately, labels visible with no delay. Acceptance: no path rests partially drawn after the section leaves view, label timing never precedes its edge, resize keeps the dash math correct, and the printed figure shows every stroke at full weight.
notes: Measure lengths after webfonts load, or reflowed text changes the SVG box and every dash value drifts.
Labels must be gated on the edge's own progress value, not a global timer, or fast scrolls desynchronise them.

title: Scroll-Scrubbed Video
description: 滚动位置驱动视频时间轴，逐帧擦洗且首帧不黑
prompt: Drive a six-second product film from scroll position instead of a playhead. Build a 300vh wrapper with a sticky 100svh stage on #08090b, and centre a 16:9 video element with muted, playsinline, preload=metadata and no controls. Re-encode the clip with a keyframe every 4 frames (or all-intra at 4Mbps for a clip this short): a one-second keyframe interval is what makes scrubbing crawl, because every seek decodes forward from the previous keyframe. Map scroll progress to currentTime inside a single requestAnimationFrame loop, quantise writes to 1/30s, and skip any assignment whose delta is under 0.02s so a fast flick does not queue dozens of seeks. On iOS, set playsinline and muted, then call play() followed by pause() once on the first user gesture, because bare currentTime assignment is ignored until playback has been unlocked; never ask for sound. Paint a poster first — frame 90 of 144 as a 1600px WebP under 45KB — set it as the video poster and keep it visible until loadedmetadata fires plus one decoded seek, so the first screen is never a black rectangle. Fallback ladder: no JavaScript and prefers-reduced-motion get the poster with a standard play button and normal playback; a decode failure or Save-Data keeps the poster static and disables the scrub rail. Add a 4px #ff5d3b rail with a 12px handle that mirrors progress, cap the video buffer at 1920px wide, and release it with removeAttribute('src') when the section unmounts. Acceptance: no seek backlog after a fast scroll, on-screen frame matches the scroll offset within 40ms, iOS plays inline without taking over the screen, and the poster stays visible until the first decoded frame arrives.
notes: Keyframe density is the entire performance story: long GOPs make every scrub a decode-from-keyframe stall.
Delta-gating currentTime is what keeps Safari from queueing seeks it cannot finish; write one value per frame at most.
currentTime and the media element are platform APIs with no licence; the MDN media guides are reference only, so nothing here is copied code.

title: Drag-to-Pan Infinite Canvas
description: 可拖拽平移的无限画布，带惯性、缩放与边界钳制
prompt: Give a project gallery a pannable canvas instead of a paginated grid. Use a 100svh viewport with overflow hidden, a #0f1116 surface and a 24px dot grid at 0.06 opacity, plus an inner layer holding 12 cards of 320x240px with 24px gaps spread across a 2400x1600 coordinate space. Implement dragging with pointerdown, setPointerCapture and pointermove, keeping the last 90ms of samples in a ring buffer; on pointerup, take the velocity of the final two samples, apply it with a 0.92 per-frame decay at 16ms steps and stop below 0.05px/ms. Clamp translation so at least 120px of content stays inside the viewport on each axis, and ease overshoot back with a 0.18 attractor rather than a hard spring. Zoom with wheel plus ctrlKey or a two-finger pinch between 0.6 and 2.2 scale, anchored on the pointer so the point under the cursor stays fixed. Keyboard: the canvas is focusable with tabindex 0 and a 2px offset focus ring; arrows pan 80px, Shift plus arrows 320px, plus and minus zoom in 0.1 steps, and Home recentres with the same 320ms easing. Pin a 44x44px reset button bottom-right, always above the canvas in z-order and never inside the transformed layer. Transform only the layer, mark cards with content-visibility: auto, and set touch-action: none on the canvas alone so page scroll still works everywhere else. Reduced motion: no inertia, 1:1 drag, zoom snaps in 0.1 increments. Acceptance: a hard drag past the edge never loses content, a flick stops without looping, pointercancel releases capture cleanly, and every control is reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
notes: Pointer capture plus a ring buffer is the whole trick; listening on window and forgetting per-pointer state is what breaks multi-touch.
Clamping after inertia, not before, is what stops the content drifting outside the viewport on a fast flick.
Pointer Events are a W3C platform API; Motion's drag gesture is MIT, so reuse is fine as long as its notice travels with the code.

title: Flip Card Deck
description: 卡组正反面三维翻转，文字不镜像且焦点跟随
prompt: Build a deck of five cards that each flip between a front and a back face when activated. Card 320x420px, 18px radius, 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.1) border, #1c1f28 fill, stacked with an 18px vertical offset and a 2deg rotation per depth level so the deck's edge is visible. Inside each card place an .inner with transform-style: preserve-3d and a 700ms transform transition on cubic-bezier(0.5,0.05,0.2,1.02); flipping to rotateY(180deg) reveals the back face, which carries backface-visibility: hidden and is pre-rotated 180deg so its text is never seen mirrored. Set perspective 1200px on the card rather than the deck, and give .inner translateZ(0) to force a composited layer. After the transition lands, run a 90ms spring settle from 176deg to 180deg so the flip reads as physical; drive it from the transitionend event rather than a hardcoded timeout. Each card is a real button with aria-pressed, a 2px visible focus ring and keyboard activation on Enter and Space; on activation move focus to the revealed heading and let Escape flip back and return focus to the button. Tap flips on coarse pointers, but a drag over 12px cancels the flip so vertical swipes still scroll the page. Fallback when 3D transforms are unsupported or prefers-reduced-motion is set: stack both faces in one grid cell, crossfade content over 200ms and rotate nothing. Acceptance: no mirrored text at any angle, flip twice returns to the exact front state, the settled transform is an exact matrix not a drifting angle, and hidden faces are never focusable or announced.
notes: Perspective on the wrong ancestor is the classic bug: it flattens the flip into a squash and looks like a scale.
Keeping the back face in the tab order is the accessibility failure here — toggle inert or visibility with the rotation.
CSS preserve-3d is a platform feature; vanilla-tilt (MIT) is useful for a subtle pointer tilt on the front face, and MIT means you can ship it while keeping its notice.

title: Spotlight Border Card
description: 指针扫过才点亮的卡片描边光弧，内容不重绘
prompt: Light a card's 1px border with a pointer-tracked spotlight while its content never repaints. Card 420x280px, 20px radius, #12141a fill on #0b0c10, with the ring drawn by a ::before at inset -1px and radius 21px: background radial-gradient(220px circle at var(--mx) var(--my), #8b5cf6, transparent 70%), the same element padded 1px, and two stacked mask layers with mask-composite: exclude (plus the -webkit- prefixed pair) so only the ring pixels survive. Update --mx and --my as percentages inside a single requestAnimationFrame callback that runs only while the pointer is inside the card, batch all reads before all writes, and stop the loop 120ms after the last move; never write custom properties directly from pointermove across six cards. Add a dimmer second glow at 0.10 opacity behind the ring for depth, and thicken the ring to 2px by scaling the pseudo-element, never by changing layout. On pointerleave, transition the gradient back to a resting rgba(255,255,255,0.10) ring over 220ms and reset the two properties to 50%. For coarse pointers, touch and prefers-reduced-motion, skip tracking entirely and show a static ring plus a 1.01 hover scale. Ship a data-spotlight off escape hatch, and keep hit area and focus ring identical whether or not the effect runs. Acceptance: content pixels never repaint while the ring moves, six cards hold 60fps, pointerleave restores the exact resting ring, and the lit ring measures at least 3:1 against the card fill.

Writing CSS variables from pointermove floods style recalc; batch them into one rAF write per frame per card.

title: Accordion Height Morph
description: 手风琴面板高度平滑展开，内容交叉淡入不跳动
prompt: Open accordion panels without the one-frame snap that toggling display produces. Build a six-row FAQ on #0a0b0f with 1px #202430 separators, 72px collapsed headers at 16px, and 18px text with a 62ch measure inside the panel. Preferred path: wrap the body in a grid whose grid-template-rows animates 0fr to 1fr over 320ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), with the inner wrapper at min-height 0 and overflow hidden, and crossfade the content from opacity 0 to 1 with a 40ms delay. Where 0fr to 1fr is unsupported or the panel holds an unpredictable media block, fall back to a measured FLIP: read scrollHeight, animate the container's inline height from 0 to that value, keep it exact when the panel content is already open, then commit height auto on transitionend and read the computed height again before closing so the reverse tween has a real start. Animate one panel at a time and close the previously open one in the same frame budget — never run three height tweens at once. The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at a panel with role=region and aria-labelledby; because the panel is never display: none, Tab reaches its links and screen readers can still measure it, while visibility toggles with a 320ms delay on close. Focus stays on the trigger through the whole morph. Reduced motion: no height animation, an instant toggle with a 120ms opacity fade. Acceptance: no cumulative height drift after fifty open and close cycles, closing works mid-animation on another panel, aria-expanded always matches what is on screen, and panel content stays in the DOM and printable.
notes: The jump comes from animating height auto; grid rows or a measured height both work, a CSS transition on auto does not.
Never remove the panel from the DOM for animation, or the content becomes invisible to assistive tech and to search.
The FLIP technique and grid-template-rows interpolation are platform CSS and Web APIs with no licence attached; no library is needed for this one.
